### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T13:27:08.240Z)

Card built. Reload `/solutions/<id>` and you'll see "Zone Balance" as the 5th analytics card.

**What's on it:**

- **Big number header**: Gini coefficient (0.00–1.00), with a colored band chip beside it that reads `Balanced` (< 0.20, green) / `Mild imbalance` (< 0.40, yellow) / `Moderate imbalance` (< 0.60, orange) / `Severe imbalance` (≥ 0.60, red).
- **Metric dropdown** in the header: `Stops` (default) / `Service time` / `Drive time`. Demand intentionally absent — per the prior conversation you confirmed stops and demand are identical in this use case.
- **Chart** (recharts `ComposedChart`):
 - Diagonal reference line (`ReferenceLine` with explicit `segment={[(0,0), (1,1)]}`) = perfect equality.
 - Lorenz curve as an `Area` (filled @ 15% opacity) + `Line` (with dots at each zone boundary) layered on top.
 - Axes 0–100% with `25%` tick stops.
- **Tooltip**: shows the zone name at that breakpoint, plus the cumulative shares (e.g. `60% of zones · 28% of work`).

**Math notes:**
- Gini computed with the standard discrete formula `G = Σ(2i−n−1)·v_i / (n·Σv)` over zones sorted ascending. Returns 0 when total is 0 or n < 2.
- Lorenz curve starts at (0,0); each subsequent point is `((i+1)/n, cum/total)`.
- Excludes the **Unzoned pseudo-bucket** — this card measures balance *across zones*, not across the full job set.
- Two empty-states: "Need 2+ zones" (single-zone case where Lorenz is trivially the diagonal) and "No work to distribute" (all metrics zero — e.g. drive time before any routes have stops in any single polygon).

**Toggleable** from Settings → Analytics like the other four cards.

Next on the roadmap was per-zone cost stacked bar. The interesting design wrinkle there is the cost-coefficient sourcing — global settings panel field, you confirmed. Want to do that next, or want to dogfood Zone Balance first?

### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T13:33:57.734Z)

Good thought. There's already a `useDistanceMatrix` hook in `libs/playground` that hits `/distancematrix/json` — same auth path, axios-based. Reusable.

Here's the shape and the tradeoff so you can pick direction before I code:

**Per-zone DM, batched:**
- For each zone: collect its in-zone stop coords, call DM with those as both origins and destinations → N×N drive-time matrix → average non-diagonal entries.
- 10 zones × ~75 stops = 10 calls. NB DM has a cell cap per request (typically 5000), so 75×75=5625 will need to split into two sub-calls per zone, or we can sample (cap at ~70 stops/zone — first N by stop order, document the truncation).
- Latency: each call ~500ms-1s; serially that's 10-20s on first load, parallel maybe 3-5s.

**Cost & UX tradeoff:**
- Auto-fetch on solution load: polished, but every page open burns DM credits, even when the user never opens the Analytics tab. Bad for the demo.
- Lazy-fetch when Analytics tab opens: better — pays for what's seen.
- Click-to-compute button: cheapest, but adds friction.

**My recommendation: hybrid.** Ship the table with a haversine-derived "Avg drive" cell as the default (~0 cost, instant, "spatial spread" estimate), with a small icon button per row (or a "Refine with real drive times" link in the card header) that triggers the DM call and replaces the value. Cached per-(solution-id, zone-id) so it sticks across re-renders. Marks the value as "estimated" vs "from network" via a subscript or color so users know which is which.

**Caching:** keyed on `{requestId, zoneId, stopCount, stopIdsHash}`. Local zustand slice + sessionStorage so toggling tabs doesn't re-hit the API.

**Truncation policy:** if a zone has > N stops where N×N exceeds the DM cap, sample uniformly to N, document the cell as "≈ from sample of X/Y stops" in the tooltip.

Three concrete questions before I code:

1. **Default load** — haversine baseline auto, DM on-click (my rec)? Or DM auto when the Analytics tab is the active tab?
2. **Speed assumption for the haversine baseline** — 30 km/h urban is the default I had in mind. Override-able in settings?
3. **What does the cell DISPLAY?** Drive time only? Drive distance only? Or both ("48 min · 12.4 km" in two lines)?

If you say "just do it, hybrid with #2 hardcoded and #3 drive time only," I'll start there. Otherwise tell me where you want to land and I'll execute.

 "content": "import {useEffect, useRef, useState} from 'react'\nimport Cookies from 'js-cookie'\nimport {useSolutionStore} from '../../../../stores/solution.store'\nimport {useUIStore} from '../../../../stores/ui.store'\n\n/**\n * Per-zone \"Avg drive time between stops\" from NB Distance Matrix.\n *\n * Auto-fires when the user is on the Analytics tab and the solution has\n * loaded. Per zone, builds a square origins=destinations matrix from the\n * zone's stop coordinates, sends a single `/distancematrix/json?mode=car`\n * request, and averages every non-diagonal cell's `duration.value` to a\n * mean drive time in minutes.\n *\n * Results are cached in-memory keyed by `(requestId, zoneId, stopIdsHash)`\n * so tab toggles don't re-hit the API. Zones with more than\n * `MAX_STOPS_PER_ZONE` stops are uniformly sampled down to keep the\n * request under NB DM's cell cap.\n */\n\n// NB DM lite cap is around 100×100 = 10000 cells. Stay conservative at\n// 100 origins × 100 destinations so a single call covers most demo\n// zones (≤100 stops) without splitting.\nconst MAX_STOPS_PER_ZONE = 100\n\n// Mirror the playground hook's environment switch — direct-to-NB call,\n// not via the BFF (which has no `/distancematrix` route).\nconst NB_BASE_URL =\n  typeof process !== 'undefined' &&\n  process.env?.['NEXT_PUBLIC_ENV'] === 'production'\n    ? 'https://api.nextbillion.io'\n    : 'https://sgpstg.nextbillion.io'\n\ntype Stop = {jobId: number; location: [number, number]}\n\nexport type ZoneDriveMatrixEntry = {\n  /** Mean drive time across all non-diagonal cells, in minutes. */\n  avgMinutes: number\n  /** Set when the zone exceeded `MAX_STOPS_PER_ZONE` and we sampled. */\n  sampled: boolean\n  sampleSize: number\n  totalStops: number\n}\n\nexport type UseZoneDriveMatrixResult = {\n  /** Map keyed by zoneId → finalized DM entry. */\n  byZoneId: Map<number, ZoneDriveMatrixEntry>\n  /** Zones currently mid-flight. */\n  loadingZones: Set<number>\n  /** Per-zone error message if the call failed. */\n  errorByZoneId: Map<number, string>\n}\n\ntype Args = {\n  /** List of zones with their job-step locations. Pass the zones you\n   *  want DM coverage for — typically the non-`Unzoned` rows of the\n   *  zone-load-summary table with stopLocations.length >= 2. */\n  zoneStops: Array<{zoneId: number; stops: Stop[]}>\n}\n\nexport function useZoneDriveMatrix({\n  zoneStops,\n}: Args): UseZoneDriveMatrixResult {\n  const mainTab = useUIStore((s) => s.mainTab)\n  const requestId = useSolutionStore((s) => s.requestId)\n\n  const [byZoneId, setByZoneId] = useState<Map<number, ZoneDriveMatrixEntry>>(\n    () => new Map(),\n  )\n  const [loadingZones, setLoadingZones] = useState<Set<number>>(\n    () => new Set(),\n  )\n  const [errorByZoneId, setErrorByZoneId] = useState<Map<number, string>>(\n    () => new Map(),\n  )\n\n  // Lives outside React state so the cache survives renders without\n  // causing them. Keyed by `${requestId}::${zoneId}::${stopIdsHash}`.\n  const cacheRef = useRef<Map<string, ZoneDriveMatrixEntry>>(new Map())\n\n  // Tracks the in-flight cache keys so two re-renders don't kick off\n  // duplicate fetches for the same zone.\n  const inFlightRef = useRef<Set<string>>(new Set())\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (mainTab !== 'analytics') return\n    if (!requestId) return\n\n    const apikey = Cookies.get('apikey')\n    if (!apikey) return\n\n    let cancelled = false\n\n    zoneStops.forEach(async ({zoneId, stops}) => {\n      if (stops.length < 2) return\n\n      const stopIdsKey = stops\n        .map((s) => s.jobId)\n        .sort((a, b) => a - b)\n        .join(',')\n      const cacheKey = `${requestId}::${zoneId}::${stopIdsKey}`\n\n      // Already cached — surface synchronously, no fetch.\n      const cached = cacheRef.current.get(cacheKey)\n      if (cached) {\n        setByZoneId((prev) => {\n          if (prev.get(zoneId) === cached) return prev\n          const next = new Map(prev)\n          next.set(zoneId, cached)\n          return next\n        })\n        return\n      }\n\n      // De-dupe parallel in-flight fetches for the same cache key.\n      if (inFlightRef.current.has(cacheKey)) return\n      inFlightRef.current.add(cacheKey)\n\n      setLoadingZones((prev) => {\n        if (prev.has(zoneId)) return prev\n        const next = new Set(prev)\n        next.add(zoneId)\n        return next\n      })\n\n      // Sample uniformly if the zone is too big for one DM call.\n      const sampled = sampleStops(stops, MAX_STOPS_PER_ZONE)\n\n      try {\n        // NB DM expects lat,lng pairs, pipe-delimited. Internal stop\n        // locations are stored lng,lat (parser convention), so swap on\n        // serialization.\n        const coordStr = sampled\n          .map((s) => `${s.location[1]},${s.location[0]}`)\n          .join('|')\n        const params = new URLSearchParams({\n          origins: coordStr,\n          destinations: coordStr,\n          mode: 'car',\n          key: apikey,\n        })\n        const url = `${NB_BASE_URL}/distancematrix/json?${params.toString()}`\n        const response = await fetch(url)\n        if (!response.ok) {\n          throw new Error(`DM ${response.status}`)\n        }\n        const json = (await response.json()) as {\n          rows?: Array<{elements?: Array<{duration?: {value?: number}}>}>\n        }\n\n        let durationSum = 0\n        let pairCount = 0\n        const rows = json.rows ?? []\n        for (let i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {\n          const elements = rows[i].elements ?? []\n          for (let j = 0; j < elements.length; j++) {\n            if (i === j) continue\n            const dur = elements[j]?.duration?.value\n            if (typeof dur === 'number' && Number.isFinite(dur) && dur > 0) {\n              durationSum += dur\n              pairCount += 1\n            }\n          }\n        }\n\n        const entry: ZoneDriveMatrixEntry = {\n          avgMinutes: pairCount > 0 ? durationSum / pairCount / 60 : 0,\n          sampled: stops.length > MAX_STOPS_PER_ZONE,\n          sampleSize: sampled.length,\n          totalStops: stops.length,\n        }\n        cacheRef.current.set(cacheKey, entry)\n        if (cancelled) return\n        setByZoneId((prev) => {\n          const next = new Map(prev)\n          next.set(zoneId, entry)\n          return next\n        })\n        setErrorByZoneId((prev) => {\n          if (!prev.has(zoneId)) return prev\n          const next = new Map(prev)\n          next.delete(zoneId)\n          return next\n        })\n      } catch (err) {\n        if (cancelled) return\n        const msg = (err as Error)?.message ?? 'Distance Matrix failed'\n        setErrorByZoneId((prev) => {\n          if (prev.get(zoneId) === msg) return prev\n          const next = new Map(prev)\n          next.set(zoneId, msg)\n          return next\n        })\n      } finally {\n        inFlightRef.current.delete(cacheKey)\n        if (!cancelled) {\n          setLoadingZones((prev) => {\n            if (!prev.has(zoneId)) return prev\n            const next = new Set(prev)\n            next.delete(zoneId)\n            return next\n          })\n        }\n      }\n    })\n\n    return () => {\n      cancelled = true\n    }\n    // Stable shape: we re-evaluate when the user lands on Analytics, the\n    // active request changes, or the input zone set/identity changes. We\n    // intentionally do NOT depend on byZoneId/loadingZones to avoid a\n    // feedback loop — cache de-dupes redundant fetches.\n    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps\n  }, [mainTab, requestId, zoneStops])\n\n  return {byZoneId, loadingZones, errorByZoneId}\n}\n\n// Uniform-stride sampler. Picks `cap` items from a list of `n` items so\n// that the chosen indices are spaced roughly evenly — gives broader\n// spatial coverage than a slice from one end.\nfunction sampleStops(stops: Stop[], cap: number): Stop[] {\n  if (stops.length <= cap) return stops\n  const out: Stop[] = []\n  const stride = stops.length / cap\n  for (let i = 0; i < cap; i++) {\n    out.push(stops[Math.floor(i * stride)])\n  }\n  return out\n}\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T13:46:10.678Z)

Done. End-to-end:

**`use-zone-aggregates.ts`**
- Dropped `totalDriveKm` / `totalDriveMinutes` and the polygon-containment segment attribution that produced empty values for depot-centric routes.
- Added `stopLocations: Array<{jobId, location}>` to each aggregate, populated during the existing route walk.
- Dropped the unused turf imports + the now-orphan `segmentZone` / `safeTurfPolygon` helpers.

**`use-zone-drive-matrix.ts`** (new, ~180 LOC)
- Reads `useUIStore(s => s.mainTab)` and `useSolutionStore(s => s.requestId)`. Fires only when `mainTab === 'analytics'` and a request is loaded.
- Per zone, builds a square `origins=destinations` string of `lat,lng` pairs and `GET`s `/distancematrix/json?mode=car&key=<apikey>` directly to NB (mirrors the playground hook's pattern — BFF doesn't proxy DM).
- Averages every non-diagonal `duration.value` to get `avgMinutes`.
- **In-memory cache** keyed by `${requestId}::${zoneId}::${sortedStopIds.join(',')}`. Tab toggles do not re-hit the API.
- **In-flight de-dupe** so two re-renders for the same zone don't kick off duplicate fetches.
- **Sampling**: zones over `MAX_STOPS_PER_ZONE` (100) are uniformly stride-sampled. Flagged on the result entry (`sampled`, `sampleSize`, `totalStops`) so a future tooltip can disclose it.
- Per-zone loading + error state surfaced separately.

**`zone-load-summary-table.tsx`**
- Drive column now reads from `driveMatrix.byZoneId.get(zoneId)?.avgMinutes`. Cell display:
 - `…` while loading (the DM call is in flight)
 - `!` if the DM call errored
 - `formatMinutes(avgMinutes)` once resolved
 - `—` if the zone has < 2 stops
- `driveMax` recomputed against the DM result so the cell mini-bar still scales correctly.
- Sort-by-Drive (column header click) now compares DM values — zones still loading sort as 0, which keeps them at the bottom in desc / top in asc (null-last).
- Compile-clean against TS.

**What you'll see when you reload:**
1. Switch to Analytics tab → DM fires for each non-empty zone in parallel.
2. Drive cells flicker `…` for ~1–2 sec, then populate with real road-network averages.
3. Network panel shows N calls to `sgpstg.nextbillion.io/distancematrix/json?mode=car&origins=...&destinations=...` (one per zone).
4. Toggle to Map and back → no re-fetch (cache hit).

**Not addressed yet (let me know if you want any of these):**
- The `…` indicator is plain text. Spinner icon would be nicer.
- Sampled-zone disclosure isn't surfaced in UI yet — the entry carries the flag, the cell just shows the value.
- DM call goes direct to NB rather than through the BFF — same as the playground hook. If your BFF gains a `/distancematrix` route later we can swap.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T15:06:03.765Z)

Done. Mirrored the preview-map approach onto the solution map:

**`use-map-layers.ts`**
- Added `TextLayer` to deck.gl imports and `useMap` + `useEffect` to React imports.
- New `useMap()` hook + `useState/useEffect` pair tracks the map's current zoom by listening to `map.on('zoom', ...)`. Lazy-initializes from `map.getZoom()` so the first paint usually has the right value; the effect re-captures post-mount in case the map wasn't ready.
- `zoneLabelData` memo computes each polygon's centroid (mean of outer-ring coords) and pairs it with the zone's `name` (falling back to `geofence_id`). Recomputes only when `zoneFeatures` changes.
- `ZONE_LABEL_HIDE_ZOOM = 13` — same threshold as the preview map. At and above that zoom, the label layer is omitted from the composed layer list.
- Inside the existing `if (showZones && zoneFeatures)` block: pushes a `v3-zone-labels` TextLayer with the same styling as the preview's (11 px bold dark-grey text, white-translucent background, centered anchor + baseline). `pickable: false` so the labels don't intercept hover events meant for the polygon underneath.
- Memo deps extended with `zoneLabelData` and `mapZoom` so the layer rebuilds on zoom crossings.

**Behavior:**
- Toggle Zones on in the solution map → polygons render with their `Zone N` (or geofence) names floating in the middle at world zooms 0–12.99.
- Zoom past 13 → labels disappear; the polygon outlines and per-zone color stay.
- Toggle Zones off → labels disappear with the polygons (they share the `showZones` gate).

### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T15:13:56.144Z)

Pre-existing errors in unrelated spec files, not my change. The v3 result panel typechecks clean.

Done. Type in the search box (`REP-001`, etc.) → matching routes auto-check.

**Behavior:**
- Non-empty query → `selectAll(filteredRoutes.map(r => r.vehicleId))` replaces the selection with whichever routes match the current filter.
- Empty query (clearing the search) → no-op. Manual selection persists, so emptying the search doesn't wipe what the user picked.
- User un-checks an auto-selected row → effect doesn't re-fire (filteredRoutes identity didn't change), so the manual uncheck sticks until the query changes again.
- Solution reload while a query is non-empty → selection refreshes to match the new dataset.

Effect deps are `[routeSearchQuery, filteredRoutes, selectAll]`. Because `filteredRoutes` is memoized against `[displayRoutes, routeSearchQuery]`, the typical case — user types — only fires on query change. Re-render churn caused by `selectAll` doesn't restart the effect because `filteredRoutes` reference is unchanged.

I limited this to the Routes tab. The Unassigned tab's filter (`filteredTasks`) isn't auto-selected because the user didn't ask for it — let me know if you want the same behavior there.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T15:24:51.605Z)

Done. Reload and the Analytics tab now reads:

**English** — Territory Load Summary · Territory Balance · "Most loaded Territory 3" · X-axis "Cumulative share of territories" · the column header "Territory".

**Localized** —
- pt-BR: Resumo de Carga por Território / Equilíbrio de Territórios / Territórios
- es-MX: Resumen de Carga por Territorio / Equilibrio de Territorios / Territorios
- fr-CA: Résumé de charge par territoire / Équilibre des territoires / Territoires

**Implementation notes:**

- **i18n strings** in all four locale files: `zoneLoadSummary`, `zoneLoadSummaryEmpty`, `zonesLabel`, `zoneCol`, `zoneBalance`, `zoneBalanceTooFewZones`, `zoneBalanceNoWork`, `axisCumZones` all updated. Adjective gender adjusted per language (e.g., `Mais carregada` → `Mais carregado` to match `território`/`territorio`/`territoire` which are masculine in PT/ES/FR).
- **Settings labels** in `utils/settings.ts` also updated so the Settings → Analytics toggle list matches the rendered card titles.
- **Per-zone display name** rewritten in `use-zone-aggregates.ts`: any zone whose upstream name matches `/^Zone (\d+)$/` becomes `Territory N`. Free-text geofence names ("Downtown") pass through unchanged. This means the KPI chip ("Most loaded Territory 3 (52)") and the Lorenz tooltip ("Territory 5") stay consistent with the column header.
- **Unzoned bucket** label switched from `Unzoned` to `No territory`.
- **i18n keys are unchanged** (still `zoneLoadSummary`, `zoneCol`, etc.) — only the human strings changed. No JSX refactor needed.

**Scoped intentionally:**
- The map's polygon labels (preview screen + solution map) still read `Zone N` because that's the upstream cluster name from `input-preview-page.tsx`. If you want those to also say `Territory N`, that's a one-line change in `normalizeInput` and `buildZones` — let me know and I'll do it.
- The **Drive** metric option in the Lorenz card was removed because the underlying total-drive aggregation is gone (replaced by the DM hook which is a per-zone average, not comparable across territories in a Lorenz sense). The card now offers Stops + Service. If you want a third dimension, I can plumb the DM averages in as a separate metric — but flag that the semantics shift from "workload balance" to "density spread."

### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T15:54:02.996Z)

The repo's canonical flow is **docker build → push → terraform apply**. Terraform reads the `image_tag` variable and updates the Cloud Run service's image URL via the `google_cloud_run_v2_service` resource. The gcloud invocation only fires inside terraform's google provider.

If you want to skip terraform and use raw `gcloud run deploy` instead (faster for one-off iteration, doesn't update terraform state):

```sh
# 0. one-time auth
gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev
gcloud config set project [GCP_PROJECT]

# 1. build + push the image (same as the README)
TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
IMAGE=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[GCP_PROJECT]/route-planner-v2/route-planner-v2-staging:$TAG

docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=https://bff-staging-[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER].us-central1.run.app \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_IAM_HOST=https://iam-stg.nextbillion.ai \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_IAM_CLIENT_ID=d9883f93-dcbc-44d5-ade8-2af69d29599d \
  -f apps/route-planner-v2/Dockerfile.staging \
  -t $IMAGE .

docker push $IMAGE

# 2. point Cloud Run at the new image (image-only update, preserves env/secrets/SA/etc.)
gcloud run services update route-planner-v2-staging \
  --image=$IMAGE \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --project=[GCP_PROJECT]
```

Notes:

- **`gcloud run services update --image=...`** is the right verb for image-only rolls on an existing service — leaves env vars, secrets, ingress, SA, scaling, etc. exactly as terraform left them. Don't use `gcloud run deploy <service>` for this: with `--image` it works the same, but if anyone omits a flag it'll start nulling out fields terraform manages.
- **State drift**: this bypasses terraform. Next time someone runs `terraform apply` with a stale `image_tag` in tfvars, it'll roll the service back to that older revision. Two ways to avoid drift:
 - Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [template[0].containers[0].image] }` to the Cloud Run resource (the README says this is intentionally NOT done).
 - Or always update tfvars to match.
- **Apple Silicon**: `--platform linux/amd64` on the docker build is mandatory — Cloud Run rejects arm64.
- **Service URL** after deploy: `gcloud run services describe route-planner-v2-staging --region=us-central1 --project=[GCP_PROJECT] --format='value(status.url)'`. Then the app is at `<url>/route-planner`.
- **Auth requirement**: you'll need `roles/run.developer` (or admin) on the project plus `roles/artifactregistry.writer` to push the image.

If you'd rather stay on the terraform-managed path (recommended for the demo since that's what the README documents and what'll match the next `apply`):

```sh
TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
IMAGE=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[GCP_PROJECT]/route-planner-v2/route-planner-v2-staging:$TAG
docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=https://bff-staging-[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER].us-central1.run.app \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_IAM_HOST=https://iam-stg.nextbillion.ai \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_IAM_CLIENT_ID=d9883f93-dcbc-44d5-ade8-2af69d29599d \
  -f apps/route-planner-v2/Dockerfile.staging -t $IMAGE .
docker push $IMAGE

cd apps/route-planner-v2/infra/terraform
terraform apply -var="image_tag=$TAG"
```

### CLAUDE (2026-06-03T17:39:45.611Z)

Looking at `job-filter-bar.tsx:67-82`, the filter already iterates across all entries in `job.time_windows` via `.some()` — each entry corresponds to one mapped time-window column pair (`time_windows_start`, `time_windows_start 1`, `time_windows_start 2`, …). So structurally it already searches every TW column.

What it does today is an **interval-overlap** test: a job is kept if any one of its TW pairs overlaps the filter range `[from, end]`. Both `from` and `end` must be satisfied by the **same** TW pair.

Two ways your ask could land — they behave differently. Which do you want?

Hidden once the user\n  // zooms past street level so the labels don't compete with individual\n  // step markers.\n  const {v3Map} = useMap()\n  const [mapZoom, setMapZoom] = useState<number>(() => {\n    const m = v3Map?.getMap?.()\n    return typeof m?.getZoom === 'function' ? m.getZoom() : 0\n  })\n  // Viewport bbox in [W,S,E,N], updated on every `move`. Drives the\n  // supercluster re-aggregation below. Same pattern the preview map uses.\n  const [mapBounds, setMapBounds] = useState<\n    [number, number, number, number] | undefined\n  >()\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const map = v3Map?.getMap?.()\n    if (!map) return\n    const onZoom = () => setMapZoom(map.getZoom())\n    const onMove = () => {\n      const b = map.getBounds()\n      setMapBounds([b.getWest(), b.getSouth(), b.getEast(), b.getNorth()])\n    }\n    map.on('zoom', onZoom)\n    map.on('move', onMove)\n    // Capture post-mount values so the initial render uses real numbers\n    // rather than the seed defaults.\n    setMapZoom(map.getZoom())\n    onMove()\n    return () => {\n      map.off('zoom', onZoom)\n      map.off('move', onMove)\n    }\n  }, [v3Map])\n\n  // ── Step pin-clustering (preview-style) ──────────────────\n  // Mirrors the preview map: a Supercluster index over step features,\n  // with `map`/`reduce` tracking whether every leaf shares the same\n  // route (vehicleId). When a cluster contains steps from one route the\n  // circle takes that route's color; when routes mix, fall back to a\n  // neutral grey so the user can read \"multi-route stack\". Cluster\n  // radius scales by point count. Individual steps that fall inside a\n  // cluster are tracked so they can be excluded from the per-step\n  // layers below — preventing visual doubling.\n  const stepSuperclusterIndex = useMemo(() => {\n    if (stepClusterFeatures.length === 0) return null\n    const index = new Supercluster({\n      radius: 60,\n      maxZoom: 14,\n      minPoints: 2,\n      map: (props: Record<string, unknown>) => ({\n        vehicleId: props.vehicleId,\n        color: props.color,\n        _mixed: false,\n      }),\n      reduce: (acc: Record<string, unknown>, next: Record<string, unknown>) => {\n        if (acc._mixed) return\n        if (acc.vehicleId !== next.vehicleId) {\n          acc.vehicleId = null\n          acc.color = null\n          acc._mixed = true\n        }\n      },\n    })\n    index.load(stepClusterFeatures as unknown as Array<unknown>)\n    return index\n  }, [stepClusterFeatures])\n\n  const {stepClusters, clusteredStepKeys} = useMemo(() => {\n    const empty = {\n      stepClusters: [] as Feature[],\n      clusteredStepKeys: new Set<string>(),\n    }\n    if (!stepSuperclusterIndex || !mapBounds) return empty\n    const z = Math.floor(mapZoom)\n    const results = stepSuperclusterIndex.getClusters(mapBounds, z)\n    const justClusters: Feature[] = []\n    const hiddenKeys = new Set<string>()\n    for (const r of results) {\n      const props = (r.properties ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>\n      if (props.cluster) {\n        justClusters.push(r)\n        const leaves = stepSuperclusterIndex.getLeaves(\n          props.cluster_id as number,\n          Infinity,\n        )\n        for (const leaf of leaves) {\n          const lp = (leaf.properties ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>\n          // Key matches the (vehicleId, stepOrder) tuple stored on each\n          // step feature — used to skip the individual marker below.\n          hiddenKeys.add(`${lp.vehicleId}::${lp.stepOrder}`)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return {stepClusters: justClusters, clusteredStepKeys: hiddenKeys}\n  }, [stepSuperclusterIndex, mapBounds, mapZoom])\n\n  // Per-cluster RGBA fill: route color when all leaves share a route,\n  // neutral grey when the cluster spans multiple routes.\n  const resolveClusterFill = (\n    feature: Feature,\n  ): [number, number, number, number] => {\n    const props = (feature.properties ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>\n    const c = props.color as [number, number, number, number] | null | undefined\n    if (Array.isArray(c) && c.length >= 3) {\n      return [c[0], c[1], c[2], 220]\n    }\n    return [120, 120, 120, 220]\n  }"

 "new_string": "  // Per-cluster RGBA fill: route color when all leaves share a route,\n  // neutral grey when the cluster spans multiple routes.\n  const resolveClusterFill = (\n    feature: Feature,\n  ): [number, number, number, number] => {\n    const props = (feature.properties ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>\n    const c = props.color as [number, number, number, number] | null | undefined\n    if (Array.isArray(c) && c.length >= 3) {\n      return [c[0], c[1], c[2], 220]\n    }\n    return [120, 120, 120, 220]\n  }\n\n  // The downstream `onStepClusterClick` handler expects the picked\n  // object to carry `isCluster`, `items`, and `clusterCount` (matching\n  // the old StepClusterLayer's picking shape).  "new_string": "  // ── Step cluster GeoJSON features (all routes) ──────────────\n  // Shared feature array fed into both:\n  //   - the Supercluster index that drives cluster circles, and\n  //   - the per-step circle+text markers (cluster + non-cluster modes).\n  // Each feature carries `text` (S / 1 / 2 / … / E), `color` (the route's\n  // RGBA), `vehicleId`, `stepOrder`, `isStartOrEnd`, and `isRest`. Rest\n  // steps (breaks/layovers) are included so they participate in cluster\n  // counts; when they fall out of a cluster they render via\n  // RestMarkerLayer (with the distinct break/layover icon) — the un-\n  // clustered rendering path below skips `isRest` features. Rest steps\n  // are only fed into the index when `showBreaksLayovers` is on, so\n  // hiding breaks also removes them from cluster counts.\n  //\n  // Regular steps at stacked locations (multiple routes sharing exact coordinates) are\n  // excluded here — they are rendered via stepStackMarkerLayer instead.\n  //\n  // hoveredStep is intentionally NOT a dependency here. Hover highlight is handled via\n  // updateTriggers on the marker layers, which lets deck.gl update styling\n  // without rebuilding the feature array or calling index.load() again.\n  const stepClusterFeatures = useMemo(() => {\n    if (!rawRoutes) return [] as Feature[]\n    const {showBreaksLayovers} = layerVisibility\n    const features: Feature[] = []\n    rawRoutes.forEach((route, routeIndex) => {\n      if (!selectedRouteIds.has(String(route.vehicle))) return\n      const vehicleId = String(route.vehicle)\n      const color = rgbToArray(routeColorGenerator(route.index ?? routeIndex))\n      const routeGeometry = route.geometry\n      const steps = route.steps ?? []\n      steps.forEach((step, stepIndex) => {\n        const isRestStep = REST_STEP_TYPES.has(step.type)\n\n        // Drop rest steps from the index when their layer is hidden so the\n        // cluster count reflects only what's actually rendered.\n        if (isRestStep && !showBreaksLayovers) return\n\n        // Steps owned by a depot are rendered by the depot marker layer\n        if (step.depot != null) return\n\n        // Resolve [lat, lng]. Rest steps are NOT subject to the stack check since\n        // they have their own distinct iconography.\n        if (\n          !isRestStep &&\n          stackedLocationKeys.has(locationKey(latLng))\n        ) {\n          return\n        }\n\n        const isStart = !isRestStep && stepIndex === 0\n        const isEnd = !isRestStep && stepIndex === steps.length - 1\n\n        let text: string\n        if (isStart) text = 'S'\n        else if (isEnd) text = 'E'\n        else text = (stepIndex + 1).toString()\n\n        const props = {\n          text,\n          color,\n          vehicleId,\n          stepOrder: stepIndex,\n          isStartOrEnd: isStart || isEnd,\n          isRest: isRestStep,\n          step: {\n            type: step.type,\n            id: step.id,\n            description: step.description,\n            arrival: step.arrival,\n            duration: step.duration,\n            service: step.service,\n            waiting_time: step.waiting_time,\n            distance: step.distance,\n            vehicle: route.vehicle,\n            timewindows: step.timewindows,\n          },\n        }\n\n        features.push(point([latLng[1], latLng[0]], props))\n      })\n    })\n    return features\n  }, [rawRoutes, selectedRouteIds, stackedLocationKeys, layerVisibility])"

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T14:28:26.403Z)

Done. Break and layover steps now participate in the supercluster.

**Summary:**

- `stepClusterFeatures` (use-map-layers.ts) now includes rest steps with `isRest: true`. Rest-step locations are resolved via the same `fillMissingStepLocation` interpolation `restMarkerFeatures` uses. Rest steps are excluded from the index when `showBreaksLayovers` is off so cluster counts reflect only what's actually rendered.
- `restMarkerFeatures` now carries `vehicleId` and `stepOrder` on each feature's `properties` so they can be keyed against `clusteredStepKeys`.
- `RestMarkerLayer` data is filtered by `clusteredStepKeys` when cluster mode is on, so rests absorbed into a cluster don't double-render.
- The un-clustered cluster-mode rendering path filters out `isRest` features (they keep their distinct break/layover iconography via `RestMarkerLayer`).
- Hover/click cluster popovers automatically include the break/layover steps too since they share the same supercluster index.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T14:33:03.062Z)

Done. The `DescriptionPanel` now auto-syncs `preferences.description` to `preferences.fileName` whenever the profile name changes — covers both `loadPreferenceConfiguration` (load) and the Configuration Name field (rename).

**Behavior:**
- Mount with `fileName='Default'`, empty description → description becomes `'Default'`.
- Load a saved profile `"Route 5 AM Shift"` → description becomes `"Route 5 AM Shift"` (overriding any description that was saved with the profile).
- Rename via Configuration Name → description follows the new name.
- User types in Description after the sync → that edit sticks until the next profile change (the effect's dep is `fileName` only, so manual description edits don't re-trigger sync).
- 200-char cap preserved (defensive `.slice(0, 200)`, though `fileName` is already capped at 40).

(Originals: 14 / 9 / 15.)\nconst START_END_RADIUS = 17.5\nconst REGULAR_STEP_RADIUS = 11.25\nconst HOVERED_STEP_RADIUS = 18.75\nconst REGULAR_TEXT_SIZE = 12.5\nconst REGULAR_TEXT_SIZE_HOVERED = 15\nconst START_END_TEXT_SIZE = 15\n\n// Per-marker label color: lift the preview map's luma-based selection\n// so pale (light) fills get a near-black label rather than the default\n// white, which disappears on pastel pinks/yellows. ITU-R BT.601 luma —\n// (0.299·R + 0.587·G + 0.114·B) — matches W3C contrast guidance closely\n// enough without the gamma-correction overhead.\nfunction resolveLabelColor(\n  rgb:\n    | [number, number, number]\n    | [number, number, number, number]\n    | null\n    | undefined,\n): [number, number, number, number] {\n  if (!rgb || rgb.length < 3) return [255, 255, 255, 255]\n  const luma = (rgb[0] * 299 + rgb[1] * 587 + rgb[2] * 114) / 1000\n  return luma > 150 ? [30, 30, 30, 255] : [255, 255, 255, 255]\n}"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T14:50:06.978Z)

All view sites filtered. Done.

**Summary:**

Added `skipLeadingRest<T>(steps)` helper to `apps/route-planner-v2/v3/features/solution/utils/step-map-utils.ts` — drops `steps[0]` when its type is `'break'` or `'layover'`; otherwise returns the array unchanged.

Applied at every view site that reads `route.steps`:
- **Map layers** (`hooks/use-map-layers.ts`) — all three iteration sites (`stepClusterFeatures`, `restMarkerFeatures`, `nonClusterStepFeatures`)
- **Manifest panel** (`components/job-list.tsx`) — the `steps` memo that feeds the timeline + drag-drop
- **Route card** (`components/result-panel.tsx`) — `adaptRawRouteToDisplayRoute`, so card counts/first/last steps reflect the filtered set
- **Timeline view** (`components/timeline/timeline-processing.ts`) — `adaptRawRouteToDomainRoute`
- **Domain transform** (`transforms/raw-to-domain.ts`) — `rawToDomainResult`, so any downstream domain consumer sees the same filtered list

`_rawRoutes` in the store stays unchanged — this is a view-layer filter only, so edits, exports, and any future operation that needs the original step sequence still has it.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T14:52:30.893Z)

Looking at the screenshot: the BREAK is step 2, right after START — so my filter (which only checks `steps[0]`) misses it. The user considers START as the route origin, not a "stop", so the BREAK at index 1 is the route's first actual stop.

Let me extend `skipLeadingRest` to also drop a rest immediately following a `start` step.


### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T14:52:41.180Z)

{
 "replace_all": false,
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/apps/route-planner-v2/v3/features/solution/utils/step-map-utils.ts",
 "old_string": "/**\n * Drop a leading break/layover from a route's step sequence. The optimizer\n * occasionally returns a rest step at index 0 (e.g. a vehicle that starts\n * its shift on a mandatory break) which makes the manifest read \"Break\"\n * before the actual start step — confusing and visually noisy on the\n * map. Hiding it keeps the route's first step the actual start.\n *\n * Generic over the step shape so both the raw API step type (uses\n * `step.type: string`) and the domain Route step type can call it.\n */\nexport function skipLeadingRest<T extends {type?: string}>(\n  steps: readonly T[],\n): T[] {\n  if (steps.length > 0 && steps[0]?.type && REST_STEP_TYPES.has(steps[0].type)) {\n    return steps.slice(1)\n  }\n  return steps as T[]\n}",
 "new_string": "/**\n * Drop a leading break/layover from a route's step sequence. The user\n * considers `start` as the route's origin marker, not a real \"stop\", so\n * a rest step immediately at index 0 OR immediately following a\n * `start` step counts as \"the first stop is a break\" and is hidden.\n *\n * Two shapes:\n *   [break, job1, job2, end]          → [job1, job2, end]\n *   [start, break, job1, job2, end]   → [start, job1, job2, end]\n *\n * Anything else (rest deeper in the route, no leading rest) is returned\n * unchanged. Generic over the step shape so both the raw API step type\n * (`step.type: string`) and the domain Route step type can call it.\n */\nexport function skipLeadingRest<T extends {type?: string}>(\n  steps: readonly T[],\n): T[] {\n  if (steps.length === 0) return steps as T[]\n  // Rest at index 0: drop it.\n  if (steps[0]?.type && REST_STEP_TYPES.has(steps[0].type)) {\n    return steps.slice(1)\n  }\n  // Start at index 0 followed by a rest at index 1: drop the rest,\n  // keep the start so the route's origin marker still renders.\n  if (\n    steps[0]?.type === 'start' &&\n    steps.length > 1 &&\n    steps[1]?.type &&\n    REST_STEP_TYPES.has(steps[1].type)\n  ) {\n    return [steps[0], ...steps.slice(2)]\n  }\n  return steps as T[]\n}"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T15:09:06.182Z)

Here's the full picture — no changes are made; this is the analysis.

## How requests are routed today

Every optimization request — from both the server-action layer (`apps/route-planner-v2/actions/server/optimization.ts`) and the v3 ky client (`v3/api/optimization.api.ts`) — uses **relative paths** (`/optimization/v2`, `/optimization/v2/result`, `/optimization/v2/get_request_input`, `/optimization/v2/create_shared_result`, `/optimization/v2/edit_routes`, `/optimization/v2/track_records`). The host is resolved from `env.getBffHost()` in v3 (`v3/api/api.ts:38`) and via `@ncc/common/server`'s fetcher in the server actions.

That host comes from env (`apps/route-planner-v2/.env.local:6-7`):

```
BFF_HOST=https://bff-staging-[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER].us-central1.run.app
NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=https://bff-staging-[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER].us-central1.run.app
```

The BFF then forwards to the actual NB API and injects the user's API key.

## Two ways to point at api.nextbillion.io

### Option A — flip the whole app to a BFF that targets prod

Easiest path. Stand up (or re-point) a BFF to api.nextbillion.io and change those env values:

```
BFF_HOST=https://<prod-bff-host>
NEXT_PUBLIC_BFF_HOST=https://<prod-bff-host>
```

Then rebuild + redeploy (the values are baked into the client bundle at build time via Dockerfile build-args — see `infra/terraform/README.md:59-65`). **Nothing else changes** in this codebase.

### Option B — bypass the BFF and hit api.nextbillion.io directly

This is what we already did for the DM call in `use-zone-drive-matrix.ts`. To do the same for optimization, the changes are:

1. **Base URL** — swap the relative path for `https://api.nextbillion.io` in each optimization call. Either replace `env.getBffHost()` per-call or build a second ky client whose `prefixUrl` is `api.nextbillion.io`.

2. **Auth shape changes from Bearer JWT → query-param API key only.** Today the v3 client (`v3/api/client.ts:74-85`) attaches both `?apiKey=<key>` AND `Authorization: Bearer <ncc_token>`. api.nextbillion.io only accepts `?key=<apikey>` — the JWT must be stripped (it'll reject on the bearer header for some endpoints, or just ignore it). The query param is named `key` on the public API, not `apiKey` — verify with the docs but in NB code we've seen both used.

3. **Drop BFF-only query params**: `caller=route-planner` and `region=<region>` are BFF idioms; the public API ignores `caller` but may reject `region`.

4. **Endpoint set shrinks dramatically.** Public api.nextbillion.io exposes:
   - `POST /optimization/v2` ✅ (create)
   - `GET /optimization/v2/result` ✅ (result)

   But these **don't exist on the public API** — they're BFF-only conveniences:
   - `/optimization/v2/get_request_input` — used to reload the input when viewing a saved solution (`v3/api/optimization.api.ts:31`)
   - `/optimization/v2/create_shared_result` — share-link generator
   - `/optimization/v2/edit_routes` — route-edit save (`v3/api/optimization.api.ts:61`)
   - `/optimization/v2/track_records` — recent solutions list (`v3/api/optimization.api.ts:87`)

   If you bypass the BFF, these features go dark unless you keep them on the BFF and only route the create+result calls to api.nextbillion.io. That's a hybrid: ~2 endpoints to prod, the rest to BFF.

5. **The base URL has to come from somewhere persistent.** Hard-code it (cheap), add a `NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_HOST` env var (clean), or per-request override via a separate ky instance.

## Recommendation

If the goal is "demo points at prod data" — **Option A** is dramatically simpler: redeploy with the prod BFF host. One env change, no auth rework, all features still work.

If the goal is "specifically these optimization calls don't go through staging BFF" (e.g., for testing prod behavior in isolation) — **Option B** is the surgical move, but accept that ~4 of the 6 optimization endpoints will break or need a fallback. Mirror the DM-call pattern: hard-code `https://api.nextbillion.io` + apiKey for the 2 supported calls, leave the rest on the BFF.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T15:14:45.719Z)

Here are the steps from your monorepo's BFF directory. They mirror the route-planner-v2 flow but with `bff-staging` as the service.

### 1. Pre-flight (one-time per machine, skip if already set up)

```sh
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/bff
gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev
gcloud config set project [GCP_PROJECT]
```

### 2. Build + push the image

```sh
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/bff

# Build the Nest dist first — Dockerfile.staging expects it.
yarn build

TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
[ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ] && TAG="${TAG}-dirty"
IMAGE=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[GCP_PROJECT]/bff/bff-staging:$TAG

# --platform linux/amd64 is required on Apple Silicon — Cloud Run rejects arm64.
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f Dockerfile.staging -t "$IMAGE" .
docker push "$IMAGE"
```

### 3. Deploy the new revision

```sh
gcloud run deploy bff-staging \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --project=[GCP_PROJECT] \
  --image="$IMAGE"
```

Cloud Run flips traffic to the new revision on the same URL (`https://bff-staging-[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER].us-central1.run.app`). No DNS, no env changes, no terraform.

### 4. Verify

After deploy completes:

```sh
# Sanity-check the deployed image
gcloud run services describe bff-staging \
  --region=us-central1 --project=[GCP_PROJECT] \
  --format='value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)'

# Tail logs while you fire an optimization request from the frontend.
# An upstream URL containing api.nextbillion.io confirms the override is live.
gcloud run services logs tail bff-staging \
  --region=us-central1 --project=[GCP_PROJECT]
```

In your application, run any optimization request from route-planner-v2 — the log line in `ApiGatewayService.send()` should now show:

```
<org> - vrj : POST https://api.nextbillion.io/optimization/v2?key=...
```

### Notes

- **Don't `terraform apply`** — the BFF terraform config sets `lifecycle.ignore_changes = [...image]` so terraform won't roll new images; only `gcloud run deploy` does. Terraform apply at this point would be a no-op for the image.
- **No env changes needed** on either side. Route-planner-v2 keeps pointing at the same `bff-staging` URL; the host swap happens inside the BFF.
- **Rollback**: if anything goes wrong, `gcloud run services update-traffic bff-staging --to-revisions=<prev-revision>=100 --region=us-central1 --project=[GCP_PROJECT]` (or just redeploy the previous tag).
- **Pre-commit**: standard caveat — the BFF change isn't committed yet; tag will be `<sha>-dirty`. Either commit first to get a clean SHA tag, or accept the `-dirty` suffix for this rev.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T15:40:52.664Z)

Done.

**`apps/route-planner-v2/v3/features/solution/hooks/use-solution-map.ts:64-95`** — replaced the "auto-enable animation for short routes" effect with:

1. **Animation forced OFF** every time a solution loads (was: enabled for routes < 500 km). User can still toggle it back on via the layer controls.
2. **Zone layer auto-enabled** when the solution's input carries any zone with geometry. Handles the load-order race: `rawInput` typically arrives after `rawRoutes`, so the effect re-fires when zone data shows up and toggles `showZones: true` exactly once per solution.

Behavior at `/route-planner/solutions/<id>`:
- Page mounts → animation off (initial state).
- Routes load → animation forced off (idempotent).
- Input loads → if any zone has geometry, zones turn on; otherwise toggle stays off (the "if available" guard).
- User toggles manually → sticks; effect doesn't re-run on layer-state changes.
- Switch to another solution → both behaviors run again for the new ID.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T15:52:30.465Z)

Got it — schema validation, not JSON. The offender: every layer has `"metadata": "group:..."` (a string), but MapLibre's style spec requires `metadata` to be an OBJECT. MapLibre's style validator throws on that during init.

Plan:
1. Change `getMapStyleUrl` to point at the new endpoint.
2. Add a `useMapStyle` hook that fetches the style, converts each layer's `metadata: "group:foo"` → `metadata: { group: "foo" }`, and returns the sanitized StyleSpecification.
3. Switch the 5 consumers from `mapStyle={getMapStyleUrl(...)}` to `mapStyle={useMapStyle(...)}`.

Kept exported for\n * any caller that wants the URL directly, but consumers feeding a Map\n * component should use `useMapStyle()` so the sanitized style object\n * is loaded — see the comment on `sanitizeStyleSpec` below.\n */\nexport function getMapStyleUrl(apiKey: string | undefined): string {\n  return `https://${MAP_HOST}${STYLE_PATH}?${STYLE_QUERY}&key=${apiKey ?? ''}`\n}\n\n/**\n * No-op now that all map requests go to api.nextbillion.io. Kept so\n * existing consumers don't break when they pass it as the Map's\n * `transformRequest` prop. If we ever need to rewrite tile/sprite\n * URLs again (e.g., to point at a staging tile server), drop the\n * rewriting logic back into this function.\n */\nexport function mapTransformRequest(url: string): {url: string} {\n  return {url}\n}\n\n/**\n * Sanitize a style spec returned by the NB-hosted TomTom endpoint.\n *\n * Workaround: every layer comes back with `\"metadata\": \"group:area\"`\n * (or similar) — a string. The MapLibre style spec requires\n * `metadata` to be an OBJECT; MapLibre's validator throws on map\n * init when it sees a string. We convert each `\"key:value\"` form to\n * `{ key: \"value\" }` so the data is preserved and the spec is met.\n *\n * Only `layers[*].metadata` is touched; sources, layout, paint, etc.\n * are returned as-is.\n */\nfunction sanitizeStyleSpec<T extends {layers?: unknown[]}>(style: T): T {\n  if (!style || !Array.isArray(style.layers)) return style\n  const layers = style.layers.map((layer) => {\n    if (!layer || typeof layer !== 'object') return layer\n    const md = (layer as {metadata?: unknown}).metadata\n    if (typeof md !== 'string') return layer\n    const colon = md.indexOf(':')\n    const fixed =\n      colon > 0\n        ? {[md.slice(0, colon)]: md.slice(colon + 1)}\n        : {value: md}\n    return {...(layer as Record<string, unknown>), metadata: fixed}\n  })\n  return {...style, layers}\n}\n\n// Module-level cache so navigating between map pages doesn't re-fetch\n// (and re-sanitize) the same ~340 KB style JSON. ## Summary

**`apps/route-planner-v2/utils/map-style.ts`** — full rewrite:
- `getMapStyleUrl` now points at `https://api.nextbillion.io/tt/style/1/style/20.3.2-3?map=basic_main&key=<apikey>`.
- `mapTransformRequest` becomes a no-op (all map requests already go to api.nextbillion.io after the BFF flip; nothing left to rewrite).
- New **`sanitizeStyleSpec(style)`** — for every layer, if `metadata` is a string like `"group:area"`, rewrites it to `{ group: "area" }` so MapLibre's style-spec validator stops complaining. The split is `<key>:<rest>` so a string with no colon still becomes a valid object (`{ value: "..." }`).
- New **`useMapStyle(apiKey)`** hook — fetches the URL, runs `sanitizeStyleSpec`, returns the StyleSpecification (or `undefined` while loading). Module-level cache keyed by URL so navigating between map screens doesn't re-fetch the ~340 KB style.

**5 consumers switched from `getMapStyleUrl` → `useMapStyle`:**
- `v3/features/solution/hooks/use-solution-map.ts` (the v3 solution page)

`getMapStyleUrl` and `mapTransformRequest` are still exported for any caller that prefers the raw URL or the transform passthrough.

We rewrite each `\"key:value\"` string to `{ key: \"value\" }` so\n// the data is preserved and the spec is met. Other endpoints (legacy\n// /maps/streets, /maps/dark, etc.) are unaffected, but we run the\n// helper unconditionally — it's a no-op when metadata isn't a string.\nfunction sanitizeStyleSpec<T extends {layers?: unknown[]}>(style: T): T {\n  if (!style || !Array.isArray(style.layers)) return style\n  const layers = style.layers.map((layer) => {\n    if (!layer || typeof layer !== 'object') return layer\n    const md = (layer as {metadata?: unknown}).metadata\n    if (typeof md !== 'string') return layer\n    const colon = md.indexOf(':')\n    const fixed =\n      colon > 0\n        ? {[md.slice(0, colon)]: md.slice(colon + 1)}\n        : {value: md}\n    return {...(layer as Record<string, unknown>), metadata: fixed}\n  })\n  return {...style, layers}\n}"

 "new_string": "// Module-level cache of fetched-and-sanitized styles, keyed by the\n// final URL (with apiKey). Avoids re-fetching ~340 KB of style JSON\n// every time the user toggles between Light → Dark → Light, and\n// shares the result across maps.\nconst styleCache = new Map<string, Promise<object>>()\n\nfunction fetchSanitizedStyle(url: string): Promise<object> {\n  let pending = styleCache.get(url)\n  if (!pending) {\n    pending = fetch(url)\n      .then((r) => {\n        if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`map style ${r.status}`)\n        return r.json()\n      })\n      .then((json) => sanitizeStyleSpec(json as {layers?: unknown[]}))\n      .catch((err) => {\n        styleCache.delete(url)\n        throw err\n      })\n    styleCache.set(url, pending)\n  }\n  return pending\n}\n\ntype MapSetStyleTarget =\n  | MapRef\n  | {setStyle: (style: string | object) => void}\n  | {getMap: () => {setStyle: (style: string | object) => void}}\n\nfunction resolveSetStyle(target: MapSetStyleTarget):\n  | ((style: string | object) => void)\n  | undefined {\n  if ('getMap' in target && typeof target.getMap === 'function') {\n    const inner = target.getMap()\n    if (inner && typeof inner.setStyle === 'function') {\n      return inner.setStyle.bind(inner)\n    }\n  }\n  if ('setStyle' in target && typeof target.setStyle === 'function') {\n    return (target.setStyle as (style: string | object) => void).bind(target)\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Apply a map style to a map instance. ### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T15:59:21.586Z)

Edits look clean.

**Why you saw the original style:**

`MapStyleSelector` (the small toggle group at the bottom of the map) runs a `useEffect` on mount that calls `map.setStyle()` with whichever option is selected — defaulting to "Light", which still pointed at `/maps/streets/style.json`. That overwrote my mount-time switch on `mapStyle={...}`.

**What I changed in `libs/route-planner-components/src/lib/components/map-style-selector.tsx`:**

1. **`MAP_VIEW_STYLE_OPTIONS`** — "Light" now points at `https://api.nextbillion.io/tt/style/1/style/20.3.2-3?map=basic_main` (the basic_main TomTom style you want). Kept Dark + Satellite as alternates; dropped the broken/Orbis entries.
2. **`sanitizeStyleSpec`** — lifted from the route-planner-v2 utils into the lib so the toggle path can use it (the lib can't import from the app).
3. **`applyMapStyle`** — was passing a URL to `setStyle`, which made MapLibre fetch the JSON itself and choke on the string-form `metadata`. Now it fetches, runs `sanitizeStyleSpec`, then calls `setStyle()` with the parsed object. Module-level cache by URL so toggling Light → Dark → Light doesn't re-fetch.
4. **`MAP_TILE_HOST`** — was env-conditional (`api.nextbillion.io` in prod, `sgpstg` elsewhere). Hardcoded to `api.nextbillion.io` to align with the BFF flip and your "all map presentations" intent.

**Stale-selection note:** if your browser has a previous map-style selection saved in localStorage that doesn't match any current option (e.g. the removed Orbis URL), the selector falls through to `styleItems[0]` = the new basic_main, so it self-heals. If you have "Dark" saved, you'll still get Dark.

Restart the Next dev server or hard-refresh; you should see the basic_main style now.

2. `filteredRoutes` rebuilds (iterates routes × steps).
3. The auto-select effect calls `selectAll(filteredRoutes.map(...))`.
4. `selectedRouteIds` change cascades into `useMapLayers` → rebuilds the supercluster index, all route polylines, depot markers, etc. **This is the heavy hit per keystroke.**

Fix: keep the input value local for instant typing feedback, and push to the store on a short debounce so the expensive filter/select chain only fires once after typing pauses.

**Summary of changes in `result-panel.tsx`:**

1. **Local input state + debounce.** A `searchInput` local state drives the `<OutlinedInput>`, with `onSearchInputChange` pushing to the Zustand store on a 150 ms debounce. 3. **External-clear sync.** If something else clears the store query (a reset elsewhere), the local input mirrors it.
4. **Cleanup.** Pending debounce timer is cleared on unmount.

End result: the input feels instant; the heavy map layer recomputation only happens once typing settles.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T16:11:49.688Z)

Two ways to approach this — pick one:

**A) Style-time filter (recommended for a known whitelist).** Modify the POI layer's `filter` expression during `sanitizeStyleSpec` so only the categories you want survive. Pros: cheapest at render time (TomTom never even tries to draw the others), works the same on every map. Cons: changes need a style re-fetch.

**B) Runtime layer filter** (`map.setFilter('POI', ...)`). Wire to a UI toggle. Pros: flip categories without re-fetching. Cons: extra plumbing; only useful if you actually want a runtime toggle.

The POI layer in this style uses `icon-image: "{icon}"` — so each feature carries an `icon` property identifying its category (TomTom's category code, e.g. `supermarket`). Filtering by `["in", ["get", "icon"], ["literal", [...]]]` is the cleanest cut.

Since you said "let's assume only supermarkets", I'll go with **A** and a whitelist that can be edited in one place. If you later want a UI control, we can add B on top.

The MapLibre style spec\n// requires `metadata` to be an object — its validator throws on map\n// init. We rewrite each `\"key:value\"` string to `{ key: \"value\" }` so\n// the data is preserved and the spec is met. Other endpoints (legacy\n// /maps/streets, /maps/dark, etc.) are unaffected, but we run the\n// helper unconditionally — it's a no-op when metadata isn't a string.\nfunction sanitizeStyleSpec<T extends {layers?: unknown[]}>(style: T): T {\n  if (!style || !Array.isArray(style.layers)) return style\n  const layers = style.layers.map((layer) => {\n    if (!layer || typeof layer !== 'object') return layer\n    const md = (layer as {metadata?: unknown}).metadata\n    if (typeof md !== 'string') return layer\n    const colon = md.indexOf(':')\n    const fixed =\n      colon > 0\n        ? {[md.slice(0, colon)]: md.slice(colon + 1)}\n        : {value: md}\n    return {...(layer as Record<string, unknown>), metadata: fixed}\n  })\n  return {...style, layers}\n}\n\n/**\n * POI categories (TomTom `icon` property values) that should remain\n * visible on the basemap. If you spot another value in the live data, add\n * it here. To restore all POIs, set this to null in the helper below.\n */\nexport const POI_ICON_WHITELIST: ReadonlyArray<string> = ['supermarket']\n\n/**\n * Restrict the basemap's POI layer to the icon categories in\n * `POI_ICON_WHITELIST` by AND-ing a category filter onto whatever\n * filter the upstream style already carries. ['all', existing, categoryFilter] : categoryFilter\n    return {...(layer as Record<string, unknown>), filter: combined}\n  })\n  return {...style, layers}\n}\n\n/**\n * Run all style transforms (metadata sanitize + POI category filter)\n * in one place so the two map-style callers (apps/route-planner-v2's\n * useMapStyle and this file's applyMapStyle) stay in sync.\n */\nfunction transformStyleSpec<T extends {layers?: unknown[]}>(style: T): T {\n  return filterPOIByCategory(sanitizeStyleSpec(style), POI_ICON_WHITELIST)\n}"

The wildcard re-export means `transformMapStyleJson` and `POI_ICON_WHITELIST` are already accessible via `@ncc/route-planner-components`. Done.

## Summary

**Approach: style-time POI filter** — modify the POI layer's `filter` expression during the same sanitize pass that already handles the metadata workaround. The basemap never even attempts to draw the unwanted icon categories.

**Changes:**

1. **`libs/route-planner-components/src/lib/components/map-style-selector.tsx`** — added:
   - `POI_ICON_WHITELIST: ReadonlyArray<string>` — exported constant. Default `['supermarket']`. Edit this list to add categories. Set to `null` in `transformStyleSpec` to disable the filter entirely.
   - `filterPOIByCategory(style, allowedIcons)` — AND-s `["in", ["get", "icon"], ["literal", allowedIcons]]` onto the existing filter of the `id: "POI"` layer. Other layers are untouched.
   - `transformStyleSpec` — pipeline that runs metadata sanitize → POI filter.
   - `transformMapStyleJson` — exported wrapper so the app's `useMapStyle` hook can use the same pipeline.
   - `fetchSanitizedStyle` now calls `transformStyleSpec` instead of raw `sanitizeStyleSpec`.

2. **`apps/route-planner-v2/utils/map-style.ts`** — replaced the local `sanitizeStyleSpec` with the imported `transformMapStyleJson` so both code paths (mount-time style + MapStyleSelector toggle) apply identical transforms.

**Result:** with `POI_ICON_WHITELIST = ['supermarket']`, only POI features whose `icon` property matches `supermarket` survive on the basemap. Everything else — hospitals, restaurants, gas stations, banks — disappears, leaving your route markers and the road network visible.

**Notes:**

- TomTom's `icon` value isn't always exactly `supermarket`. If after restart you're seeing fewer/no POIs than expected, open devtools, inspect a vector tile feature, and check the actual `icon` string — then add it (or its plural / synonym) to `POI_ICON_WHITELIST`. Common candidates: `supermarket`, `grocery_store`, `convenience_store`.
- Cache is keyed by URL, so changing the whitelist requires a page reload (or in dev, the HMR will rebuild).
- For a runtime UI toggle later, the same `filterPOIByCategory` logic could be re-applied via `map.setFilter('POI', newFilter)` without re-fetching — happy to wire that when needed.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T16:20:46.281Z)

Done.

**`apps/route-planner-v2/v3/features/solution/hooks/use-map-layers.ts:429-447`** — `onZoneHoverWrapped` no longer forwards the hover to `hoverHandlers.onZoneHover`, which is what was setting `popupType: 'zone'` and triggering the dark "Zone ID / Zone Name" infowindow. Now it just:

## Summary

**`apps/route-planner-v2/v3/features/solution/hooks/use-map-layers.ts`** — added a single zoom-threshold gate (`STEP_MARKER_MIN_ZOOM = 10`) and AND-ed it into every step-marker layer push:

- Step pin-clusters + count labels
- Per-step circle+text markers (regular + start/end, both cluster-mode and non-cluster-mode branches)
- Step-stack pills
- Rest markers (breaks/layovers)

What stays visible below the threshold:
- Route polylines (the main story at regional zoom)
- Zone polygons + their in-polygon labels
- Depots (kept on purpose — useful anchor for where each route starts/ends)
- Unassigned-task markers (separate layer, not gated)

At regional zoom you'll now see clean polylines through the zones with depots and zone labels marking the structure. Pan in past city level (zoom ≥ 10) and the step markers / clusters / pills come back automatically. If 10 feels too aggressive or too lenient when you try it, tweak the `STEP_MARKER_MIN_ZOOM` constant.

### USER (2026-06-04T18:21:55.361Z)

any additional suggestions for analytics panel that highlights the zone/territory planning


### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T18:22:40.226Z)

You've already got the Load Summary table + Lorenz/Gini for distribution. Strongest additions for territory planning specifically, grouped by what each answers:

**Shape quality** — is this territory drawn well?
1. **Compactness score** per territory (Polsby-Popper: `4π·area / perimeter²`). A small KPI tile per zone with a 0–1 score; long-thin or fjord-shaped territories surface immediately as candidates for redraw.
2. **Drive-to-service ratio** per territory. Driving time as % of total route time. A high ratio = the territory shape is forcing long traversals between stops. Pairs naturally with the Lorenz card to show *why* one territory is heavy.

**Assignment vs reality** — are routes respecting boundaries?
3. **Boundary-crossing index** — count + percentage of route segments where consecutive stops live in different territories. Each territory pair gets a number; high-cross-traffic pairs suggest the boundary is in the wrong place.
4. **Cross-territory flow Sankey** (you flagged this before; worth implementing). Bands connecting territory pairs, width = stops or distance flowing between them. Same data as #3 but visual.

**Match supply to demand**
5. **Capacity vs demand per territory** — grouped bar: vehicle capacity available (sum of vehicle capacities entering) next to demand (sum of stop demands). Imbalances are bright red and obvious.
6. **Vehicles entering per territory** with per-vehicle stop count alongside. Catches the case where one territory needs 4 trucks but is over-served by 6.

**Multi-day patterns** — for the 6DAY_PLAN data you've been using
7. **Heatmap: territory × day** — rows are territories, columns are days (MON–SAT), cell color = stop count. Spot territories that get hammered on Friday and ignored on Monday at a glance.
8. **Visit frequency per territory** — for the multi-day plan, average visits-per-week per stop in each territory. Highlights service consistency.

**Business mix**
9. **Stop category breakdown per territory** — your demo data already has prefixes (`BAR-`, `POSTO-`, `REST-`, `MERC-`, etc.). Stacked horizontal bar per territory showing the mix. Lets a planner say "Territory 3 is 80% bars, Territory 5 is 60% gas stations" — useful when sales reps specialize.

**Sanity checks (cheap to build, high signal)**
10. **Unzoned stops** — if any selected stops fall outside every territory polygon, that's almost always a data bug. A tiny card with "N stops outside any territory" + click-to-zoom resolves a class of mystery issues fast.
11. **Stops per km² per territory** — single column added to the existing Load Summary table. Density immediately answers "are some reps walking around a parking lot while others drive 80km between stops?"

If I had to pick the three with the highest demo punch for FEMSA-style territory planning, I'd go: **boundary-crossing index (#3) + Sankey (#4)** as a pair, **capacity vs demand (#5)**, and the **territory × day heatmap (#7)**. Together they cover "is the territory shape right", "is the resourcing right", and "is the schedule right" — the three questions a planner is actually trying to answer.

Want me to build any of these? They're all additive cards in the existing analytics registry pattern.

 "content": "import {useMemo} from 'react'\nimport type {Route, RouteStep} from '../../../../domain/types/route'\nimport type {OptimizationMvrpOrderJobV2} from '../../../../api/types/optimization.types'\n\n/**\n * Walks each selected route's step sequence once, classifies every\n * consecutive job→job pair as \"same territory\" or \"crossing\", and\n * returns both the totals and a per-pair breakdown.\n *\n * Boundary-Crossing card (#3) renders the totals + sorted pair list.\n * Cross-Territory Flow Sankey (#4) renders the same per-pair data as\n * nodes + links. Sharing the compute step keeps the two cards in sync.\n *\n * \"Job step\" = pickup/delivery/job (start, end, break, layover are\n * skipped — they don't represent a service visit, so a hop between\n * the depot start and the first job isn't a \"territory crossing\" in\n * any meaningful sense). Zone assignment comes from\n * `input.jobs[].zones[0]` — the same logical assignment used by\n * `useZoneAggregates`, so the two cards agree on what zone a stop\n * belongs to.\n */\n\nconst JOB_STEP_TYPES = new Set(['job', 'pickup', 'delivery'])\nconst isJobStep = (s: RouteStep): boolean => JOB_STEP_TYPES.has(s.type)\n\nexport type ZoneKey = number | '__unzoned__'\n\nexport type CrossingPair = {\n  fromZone: ZoneKey\n  toZone: ZoneKey\n  count: number\n}\n\nexport type ZoneCrossings = {\n  /** Total job→job transitions inspected (denominator). */\n  totalTransitions: number\n  /** Subset where fromZone !== toZone. */\n  totalCrossings: number\n  /** Crossings ÷ transitions (0..1). */\n  crossingShare: number\n  /** Per-pair counts, sorted by count DESC. Both directions of a\n   *  zone pair are kept distinct since direction can matter (e.g.,\n   *  reps that \"fan out\" from a hub territory). */\n  pairs: CrossingPair[]\n}\n\ntype Args = {\n  routes: Route[]\n  jobs: OptimizationMvrpOrderJobV2[] | undefined\n}\n\nexport function useZoneCrossings({routes, jobs}: Args): ZoneCrossings {\n  return useMemo(() => computeZoneCrossings({routes, jobs}), [routes, jobs])\n}\n\nfunction computeZoneCrossings({\n  routes,\n  jobs,\n}: Args): ZoneCrossings {\n  const jobZoneIndex = new Map<number, ZoneKey>()\n  ;(jobs ?? []).forEach((job) => {\n    const raw = (job.zones as unknown as Array<string | number> | undefined)?.[0]\n    if (raw === undefined || raw === null || raw === '') {\n      jobZoneIndex.set(job.id, '__unzoned__')\n      return\n    }\n    const asNum = typeof raw === 'number' ? raw : Number.parseInt(String(raw), 10)\n    jobZoneIndex.set(job.id, Number.isFinite(asNum) ? asNum : '__unzoned__')\n  })\n\n  const pairCounts = new Map<string, CrossingPair>()\n  const pairKey = (from: ZoneKey, to: ZoneKey) => `${from}|${to}`\n\n  let totalTransitions = 0\n  let totalCrossings = 0\n\n  for (const route of routes) {\n    let prevZone: ZoneKey | null = null\n    for (const step of route.steps) {\n      if (!isJobStep(step)) continue\n      const zone =\n        jobZoneIndex.get(step.id) ?? ('__unzoned__' as ZoneKey)\n      if (prevZone !== null) {\n        totalTransitions++\n        if (prevZone !== zone) {\n          totalCrossings++\n          const key = pairKey(prevZone, zone)\n          const existing = pairCounts.get(key)\n          if (existing) {\n            existing.count++\n          } else {\n            pairCounts.set(key, {fromZone: prevZone, toZone: zone, count: 1})\n          }\n        }\n      }\n      prevZone = zone\n    }\n  }\n\n  const pairs = Array.from(pairCounts.values()).sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count)\n  const crossingShare =\n    totalTransitions > 0 ? totalCrossings / totalTransitions : 0\n\n  return {\n    totalTransitions,\n    totalCrossings,\n    crossingShare,\n    pairs,\n  }\n}\n"
}

 />\n                    <span className={styles.zoneName}>{labelFor(p.toZone)}</span>\n                  </div>\n                  <div className={styles.pairBarTrack}>\n                    <div\n />\n                  </div>\n                  <div className={styles.pairCount}>{p.count}</div>\n                </div>\n              ))}\n              {remainder > 0 && (\n                <div className={styles.more}>\n                  +{remainder} {t('morePairs')}\n                </div>\n              )}\n            </div>\n          )}\n        </>\n      )}\n    </AnalyticsCard>\n Built from the same per-pair data as the Boundary-\n * Crossing card; thick ribbons mark heavy traffic between specific\n * pairs and immediately surface mis-shaped boundaries.\n *\n * Each territory appears twice in the diagram — once on the LEFT\n * (origin) and once on the RIGHT (destination) — so a route hopping\n * back and forth between two zones lights both directions. To keep\n * the diagram from collapsing into a single straight ribbon, we\n * preserve direction in the link data.\n */\n\nexport function TerritoryFlowCard({\n  routes,\n  jobs,\n  zones,\n  isPrimary,\n}: AnalyticsProps) {\n  const t = useTranslations('analytics')\n  const {pairs, totalCrossings} = useZoneCrossings({routes, jobs})\n\n  const zoneNameById = useMemo(() => {\n    const map = new Map<number, string>()\n    ;(zones ?? []).forEach((z) => {\n      const raw = z.name ?? `Zone ${z.id}`\n      const m = /^Zone\\s+(\\d+)$/.exec(raw)\n      map.set(z.id, m ? `Territory ${m[1]}` : raw)\n    })\n    return map\n  }, [zones])\n\n  const sankeyData = useMemo(() => {\n    if (pairs.length === 0) return null\n\n    // Build node list: each zone has a LEFT (source) and RIGHT\n    // (target) node so direction is preserved in the diagram.\n    // Recharts Sankey requires nodes referenced by numeric index.\n    const seen = new Map<string, number>()\n    const nodes: Array<{name: string; color: string; key: ZoneKey}> = []\n    const getNodeIndex = (zone: ZoneKey, side: 'L' | 'R'): number => {\n      const k = `${zone}|${side}`\n      const cached = seen.get(k)\n      if (cached != null) return cached\n      const idx = nodes.length\n      const label =\n        zone === '__unzoned__'\n          ? t('noTerritory')\n          : zoneNameById.get(zone) ?? `Territory ${zone}`\n      const [r, g, b] =\n        zone === '__unzoned__'\n          ? [120, 120, 120]\n          : zoneColorGenerator(zone).border\n      nodes.push({name: label, color: `rgb(${r}, ${g}, ${b})`, key: zone})\n      seen.set(k, idx)\n      return idx\n    }\n    const links = pairs.map((p) => ({\n      source: getNodeIndex(p.fromZone, 'L'),\n      target: getNodeIndex(p.toZone, 'R'),\n      value: p.count,\n    }))\n    return {nodes, links}\n  }, [pairs, zoneNameById, t])\n\n  if (!sankeyData || sankeyData.links.length === 0) {\n    return (\n      <AnalyticsCard\n        title={t('territoryFlow')}\n        icon={<AccountTreeOutlinedIcon />}\n        isPrimary={isPrimary}\n      >\n        <div className={styles.empty}>{t('territoryFlowEmpty')}</div>\n      </AnalyticsCard>\n    )\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <AnalyticsCard\n      title={t('territoryFlow')}\n      icon={<AccountTreeOutlinedIcon />}\n      isPrimary={isPrimary}\n    >\n      <div className={styles.subtitle}>\n        {totalCrossings.toLocaleString()} {t('totalCrossings')}\n      </div>\n      <div className={styles.chartWrap}>\n        <ResponsiveContainer width=\"100%\" height={isPrimary ? 280 : 360}>\n          <Sankey\n            data={sankeyData}\n            // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any\n            node={(props: any) => (\n              <SankeyNode {...props} fill={sankeyData.nodes[props.index]?.color} />\n            )}\n            // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any\n            link={(props: any) => (\n              <SankeyLink\n                {...props}\n                fill={sankeyData.nodes[props.payload.source.index]?.color}\n              />\n            )}\n            margin={{top: 8, right: 100, bottom: 8, left: 100}}\n            nodePadding={12}\n          >\n            <RechartsTooltip content={<FlowTooltip />} />\n          </Sankey>\n        </ResponsiveContainer>\n      </div>\n    </AnalyticsCard>\n  )\n}\n\n// ── Sankey node + link renderers ─────────────────────────────────\n\nfunction SankeyNode(props: {\n  x: number\n  y: number\n  width: number\n  height: number\n  payload: {name: string; value: number}\n  fill?: string\n}) {\n  const {x, y, width, height, payload, fill} = props\n  const isLeftSide = x < 200 // crude: nodes on the left half are origins\n  return (\n    <g>\n      <rect\n        x={x}\n        y={y}\n        width={width}\n        height={height}\n        fill={fill ?? '#1e55de'}\n        fillOpacity={0.85}\n      />\n      <text\n        x={isLeftSide ? x - 6 : x + width + 6}\n        y={y + height / 2}\n        fontSize={11}\n        fill=\"#1a1a2e\"\n        textAnchor={isLeftSide ? 'end' : 'start'}\n        dominantBaseline=\"middle\"\n      >\n        {payload.name}\n      </text>\n    </g>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction SankeyLink(props: {\n  sourceX: number\n  sourceY: number\n  sourceControlX: number\n  targetControlX: number\n  targetX: number\n  targetY: number\n  linkWidth: number\n  fill?: string\n}) {\n  const {\n    sourceX,\n    sourceY,\n    sourceControlX,\n    targetControlX,\n    targetX,\n    targetY,\n    linkWidth,\n    fill,\n  } = props\n  return (\n    <path\n      d={`M${sourceX},${sourceY} C${sourceControlX},${sourceY} ${targetControlX},${targetY} ${targetX},${targetY}`}\n      stroke={fill ?? '#1e55de'}\n      strokeWidth={linkWidth}\n      strokeOpacity={0.35}\n      fill=\"none\"\n    />\n  )\n}\n\nfunction FlowTooltip(props: {\n  active?: boolean\n  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any\n  payload?: Array<{payload: any}>\n}) {\n  const t = useTranslations('analytics')\n  if (!props.active || !props.payload?.length) return null\n  const p = props.payload[0].payload\n  // Sankey tooltip fires for both nodes and links; differentiate by shape.\n  if (p.source && p.target) {\n    const fromName = p.source.name ?? ''\n    const toName = p.target.name ?? ''\n    return (\n      <div className={styles.tooltip}>\n        <div className={styles.tooltipLabel}>\n          {fromName} → {toName}\n        </div>\n        <div className={styles.tooltipRow}>\n          <span>{t('transitionsLabel')}</span>\n          <strong>{p.value?.toLocaleString?.() ?? p.value}</strong>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n    )\n  }\n  return (\n    <div className={styles.tooltip}>\n      <div className={styles.tooltipLabel}>{p.name}</div>\n      <div className={styles.tooltipRow}>\n        <span>{t('flowVolume')}</span>\n        <strong>{p.value?.toLocaleString?.() ?? p.value}</strong>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n"
}

If the demo carries multi-dim\n * capacities, the first dimension is what we show.\n */\n\nconst QUANTITY_DIMENSION = 0\nconst JOB_STEP_TYPES = new Set(['job', 'pickup', 'delivery'])\nconst isJobStep = (s: RouteStep): boolean => JOB_STEP_TYPES.has(s.type)\n\nexport function CapacityVsDemandCard({\n  routes,\n  jobs,\n  vehicles,\n  zones,\n  isPrimary,\n}: AnalyticsProps) {\n  const t = useTranslations('analytics')\n  const {aggregates} = useZoneAggregates({routes, jobs, vehicles, zones})\n\n  // Capacity by territory: sum of capacity[QD] for unique vehicles\n  // whose routes touch at least one stop in the territory.\n  const capacityByZone = useMemo(() => {\n    const vehicleCapacity = new Map<string, number>()\n    ;(vehicles ??
