[]).forEach((job) => {\n      const raw = (job.zones as unknown as Array<string | number> | undefined)?.[0]\n      if (raw === undefined || raw === null || raw === '') {\n        jobZone.set(job.id, '__unzoned__')\n        return\n      }\n      const asNum = typeof raw === 'number' ? raw : Number.parseInt(String(raw), 10)\n      jobZone.set(job.id, Number.isFinite(asNum) ? asNum : '__unzoned__')\n    })\n\n    // zoneId → Set<vehicleId>, then sum capacity from the resulting set.\n    const seenVehicles = new Map<number | '__unzoned__', Set<string>>()\n    for (const route of routes) {\n      for (const step of route.steps) {\n        if (!isJobStep(step)) continue\n        const z = jobZone.get(step.id) ?? '__unzoned__'\n        let set = seenVehicles.get(z)\n        if (!set) {\n          set = new Set()\n          seenVehicles.set(z, set)\n        }\n        set.add(route.vehicleId)\n      }\n    }\n\n    const out = new Map<number | '__unzoned__', number>()\n    seenVehicles.forEach((set, zone) => {\n      let sum = 0\n      set.forEach((vid) => {\n        sum += vehicleCapacity.get(vid) ?? 0\n      })\n      out.set(zone, sum)\n    })\n    return out\n  }, [routes, jobs, vehicles])\n\n  const chartData = useMemo(() => {\n    return aggregates\n      .filter((a) => !a.isUnzoned)\n      .map((a) => {\n        const cap = capacityByZone.get(a.zoneId as number) ?? 0\n        return {\n          zoneId: a.zoneId as number,\n          name: a.zoneName,\n          demand: a.totalDemand,\n          capacity: cap,\n          gap: cap - a.totalDemand,\n          color: rgbCss(a.color),\n        }\n      })\n  }, [aggregates, capacityByZone])\n\n  if (chartData.length === 0) {\n    return (\n      <AnalyticsCard\n        title={t('capacityVsDemand')}\n        icon={<BalanceOutlinedIcon />}\n        isPrimary={isPrimary}\n      >\n        <div className={styles.empty}>{t('capacityVsDemandEmpty')}</div>\n      </AnalyticsCard>\n    )\n  }\n\n  const overSupplied = chartData.filter((d) => d.capacity > d.demand * 1.5).length\n  const underSupplied = chartData.filter((d) => d.capacity < d.demand * 0.8).length\n\n  return (\n    <AnalyticsCard\n      title={t('capacityVsDemand')}\n      icon={<BalanceOutlinedIcon />}\n      isPrimary={isPrimary}\n    >\n      <div className={styles.header}>\n        <div className={styles.kpiRow}>\n          <div className={styles.kpiBox}>\n            <span className={styles.kpiNumber}>{underSupplied}</span>\n            <span className={`${styles.kpiTag} ${styles.bad}`}>\n              {t('underSupplied')}\n            </span>\n          </div>\n          <div className={styles.kpiBox}>\n            <span className={styles.kpiNumber}>{overSupplied}</span>\n            <span className={`${styles.kpiTag} ${styles.warn}`}>\n              {t('overSupplied')}\n            </span>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n      <div className={styles.chartWrap}>\n        <ResponsiveContainer width=\"100%\" height={isPrimary ? 280 : 320}>\n          <BarChart\n            data={chartData}\n            margin={{top: 8, right: 16, bottom: 24, left: 12}}\n          >\n            <CartesianGrid strokeDasharray=\"3 3\" stroke=\"#eef0f5\" />\n            <XAxis\n              dataKey=\"name\"\n              tick={{fontSize: 11, fill: '#6b7280'}}\n              interval={0}\n              angle={-25}\n              textAnchor=\"end\"\n              height={48}\n            />\n            <YAxis tick={{fontSize: 11, fill: '#6b7280'}} />\n            <RechartsTooltip content={<CapacityTooltip />} />\n            <Legend\n              wrapperStyle={{fontSize: 12, paddingTop: 4}}\n              iconType=\"circle\"\n            />\n            <Bar\n              dataKey=\"demand\"\n              name={t('demand')}\n              fill=\"#1e55de\"\n              radius={[3, 3, 0, 0]}\n              isAnimationActive={false}\n            />\n            <Bar\n              dataKey=\"capacity\"\n              name={t('capacity')}\n              fill=\"#16a34a\"\n              radius={[3, 3, 0, 0]}\n              isAnimationActive={false}\n            />\n          </BarChart>\n        </ResponsiveContainer>\n      </div>\n    </AnalyticsCard>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction rgbCss(c: [number, number, number, number]): string {\n  return `rgb(${c[0]}, ${c[1]}, ${c[2]})`\n}\n\nfunction CapacityTooltip(props: {\n  active?: boolean\n  payload?: Array<{\n    payload: {\n      name: string\n      demand: number\n      capacity: number\n      gap: number\n    }\n  }>\n}) {\n  const t = useTranslations('analytics')\n  if (!props.active || !props.payload?.length) return null\n  const p = props.payload[0].payload\n  const ratio = p.demand > 0 ? p.capacity / p.demand : Infinity\n  return (\n    <div className={styles.tooltip}>\n      <div className={styles.tooltipLabel}>{p.name}</div>\n      <div className={styles.tooltipRow}>\n        <span>{t('demand')}</span>\n        <strong>{p.demand.toLocaleString()}</strong>\n      </div>\n      <div className={styles.tooltipRow}>\n        <span>{t('capacity')}</span>\n        <strong>{p.capacity.toLocaleString()}</strong>\n      </div>\n      <div className={styles.tooltipRow}>\n        <span>{t('coverage')}</span>\n        <strong>\n          {Number.isFinite(ratio) ? `${(ratio * 100).toFixed(0)}%` : '—'}\n        </strong>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n"
}

[]).forEach((job) => {\n      const raw = (job.zones as unknown as Array<string | number> | undefined)?.[0]\n      if (raw === undefined || raw === null || raw === '') {\n        jobZone.set(job.id, '__unzoned__')\n        return\n      }\n      const asNum = typeof raw === 'number' ? raw : Number.parseInt(String(raw), 10)\n      jobZone.set(job.id, Number.isFinite(asNum) ? asNum : '__unzoned__')\n    })\n\n    // zoneId metadata (name + color)\n    const zoneById = new Map<\n      number,\n      {name: string; color: [number, number, number, number]}\n    >()\n    ;(zones ?? Sun = 6\n        // for an ISO-style week layout.\n        const dow = d.day()\n        const col = dow === 0 ? 6 : dow - 1\n        const zone = jobZone.get(step.id) ?? '__unzoned__'\n        const r = getRow(zone)\n        r[col] += 1\n        if (r[col] > maxCell) maxCell = r[col]\n      }\n    }\n\n    const out = Array.from(rows.entries())\n      .filter(([key]) => {\n        // Suppress an empty unzoned row — adds clutter when every job\n        // does have a territory. Empty real zones stay (deliberate\n        // signal that the territory was skipped that period).\n        if (key !== '__unzoned__') return true\n        const cells = rows.get(key)!\n        return cells.some((n) => n > 0)\n      })\n      .map(([key, cells]) => {\n        const meta =\n          key === '__unzoned__'\n            ? {name: t('noTerritory'), color: [120, 120, 120, 255] as [number, number, number, number]}\n            : zoneById.get(key as number) ?? {\n                name: `Territory ${key}`,\n                color: [120, 120, 120, 255] as [number, number, number, number],\n              }\n        const total = cells.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)\n        return {key, name: meta.name, color: meta.color, cells, total}\n      })\n      .sort((a, b) => {\n        if (a.key === '__unzoned__') return 1\n        if (b.key === '__unzoned__') return -1\n        return (a.key as number) - (b.key as number)\n      })\n\n    return {rows: out, maxCell}\n  }, [routes, jobs, zones, dispatchTimezone, t])\n\n  if (data.rows.length === 0 || data.maxCell === 0) {\n    return (\n      <AnalyticsCard\n        title={t('territoryDayHeatmap')}\n        icon={<GridViewOutlinedIcon />}\n        isPrimary={isPrimary}\n      >\n        <div className={styles.empty}>{t('territoryDayHeatmapEmpty')}</div>\n      </AnalyticsCard>\n    )\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <AnalyticsCard\n      title={t('territoryDayHeatmap')}\n      icon={<GridViewOutlinedIcon />}\n      isPrimary={isPrimary}\n    >\n      <div className={styles.tableWrap}>\n        <table className={styles.heatmap}>\n          <thead>\n            <tr>\n              <th className={styles.zoneCol} />\n              {DAY_KEYS.map((dk) => (\n                <th key={dk} </thead>\n          <tbody>\n            {data.rows.map((row) => (\n              <tr key={row.key}>\n                <th className={styles.zoneCell}>\n                  <span\n    </th>\n                {row.cells.map((n, i) => (\n                  <td\n                    key={i}\n                    className={styles.heatCell}\n                    style={cellStyle(n,    </div>\n    </AnalyticsCard>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction rgbCss(c: [number, number, number, number]): string {\n  return `rgb(${c[0]}, ${c[1]}, ${c[2]})`\n}\n\nfunction cellStyle(n: number, max: number): ### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T18:35:50.786Z)

All four cards are built. Summary:

**New files (8):**

- `use-zone-crossings.ts` — shared helper that walks routes once and produces transition + per-pair counts. Used by #3 and #4 so they agree on the data.
- `boundary-crossing-card.tsx` + `.module.scss` — #3
- `territory-flow-card.tsx` + `.module.scss` — #4 (Recharts `Sankey` with custom node/link renderers; territory-colored ribbons)
- `capacity-vs-demand-card.tsx` + `.module.scss` — #5 (grouped bar chart; "under-supplied" / "over-supplied" KPI tiles up top using 0.8× and 1.5× thresholds)
- `territory-day-heatmap-card.tsx` + `.module.scss` — #7 (HTML table with sequential blue-ramp cells; uses `step.arrival` + dispatch timezone)

**Updated:**

- `analytics-view.tsx` — registered the four new components.
- `utils/settings.ts` — added entries 6-9 (all `enabled: true` by default).
- `messages/en.json`, `es-MX.json`, `pt-BR.json`, `fr-CA.json` — added ~25 new `analytics.*` keys per locale (validated JSON in all four).

**Design notes:**

- **Boundary-crossing** uses Lorenz/Gini-style colored bands: `< 10%` good, `< 20%` mild, `< 35%` warn, else bad. Tune those thresholds in `bandFor()` if your domain is stricter or looser about boundary leakage.
- **Sankey** preserves direction (each territory appears as a LEFT origin node and RIGHT destination node) so back-and-forth pairs read clearly. If the dataset is bushy you may want to switch to a top-N or merge-by-pair view — easy follow-up.
- **Capacity vs demand** counts each vehicle's capacity once per territory it touches. If a single vehicle visits 5 territories its full capacity is added to *all five* totals. That matches how a planner thinks about "how much capacity is available to a territory", but if you want strict per-territory apportionment (capacity ÷ N territories visited) that's a one-line change.
- **Territory × Day heatmap** uses `dayjs` with the dispatch timezone from `vehicles[0].metadata.ncc_dispatch_timezone` (same source the route panel uses). Day-of-week is Mon-first to match ISO weeks. Empty cells (territory got no work that day) render light grey so the "skipped Friday" pattern jumps out.

Each card is gated by `selectedRouteIds.size > 0` via the existing analytics-view logic, so they automatically respect the routes-filter you already use elsewhere.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T23:14:22.182Z)

Looking at the current flow: there's a global "Edit" button that puts the whole table into edit mode. The user wants per-cell editability without flipping that switch.

Approach: double-click any cell to edit just that cell (Excel-style). Blur or Enter commits, Escape cancels. The whole-table Edit button stays for bulk changes; this is additive.

 "new_string": "  const onCopyAttributeColumn = (columnIndex: number, rowIndex: number) => {\n    dispatch.inputCore.copyAttributeColumn(inputType, {\n      columnIndex,\n      rowIndex,\n    })\n  }\n\n  // Begin ad-hoc edit of a single cell. Captures the current value so\n  // Escape can restore it, then puts the cell into the same focused/\n  // editing state the bulk-edit mode uses (so the existing onCellChange\n  // useEffect commits on blur).\n  const startAdhocEdit = (\n    rowIndex: number,\n    columnIndex: number,\n    currentValue: string,\n  ) => {\n    if (isEditing) return // bulk mode already covers the whole table\n    adhocOriginalRef.current = currentValue\n    setEdittingValue(currentValue)\n    setAdhocCell({row: rowIndex, col: columnIndex})\n    setEdittingCell({row: rowIndex, col: columnIndex})\n  }\n\n  // Escape from ad-hoc edit — discards the in-flight value by\n  // restoring the snapshot, then exits both the ad-hoc and the\n  // focused-cell state. The commit useEffect still fires because\n  // edittingCell resets to (-1, -1), but it dispatches the restored\n  // (original) value, which is a no-op against the underlying row.\n  const cancelAdhocEdit = () => {\n    setEdittingValue(adhocOriginalRef.current)\n    adhocOriginalRef.current = ''\n    setAdhocCell(null)\n    setEdittingCell({row: -1, col: -1})\n  }\n\n  // Blur / commit path — same as bulk-edit blur, just also clears\n  // the ad-hoc marker so the cell flips back to read-only mode.\n  const commitAdhocEdit = () => {\n    adhocOriginalRef.current = ''\n    setAdhocCell(null)\n    setEdittingCell({row: -1, col: -1})\n  }"

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T23:17:27.721Z)

Wiring is in place end-to-end. Summary of the implementation:

**`apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/data-mapper/data-mapper-table.tsx`**
- New per-cell state: `adhocCell: {row, col} | null` and `adhocOriginalRef` (snapshot for Escape).
- Three handlers: `startAdhocEdit` (records snapshot + activates cell), `cancelAdhocEdit` (restores snapshot → effectively a no-op dispatch), `commitAdhocEdit` (clears ad-hoc marker; existing blur-commit useEffect still dispatches the new value).
- Threaded `isAdhocEditing` + the three handlers through to each `DataMapperCell`.
- Guard: `startAdhocEdit` short-circuits when the table-wide Edit toggle is already on, so bulk mode behavior is unchanged.

**`apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/data-mapper/data-mapper-cell.tsx`**
- New optional props on `DataMapperCell`: `isAdhocEditing`, `onStartAdhocEdit`, `onCancelAdhocEdit`, `onCommitAdhocEdit`. All optional so other call sites compile unchanged.
- `showEditor = isEditing || isAdhocEditing` — both paths render the same `<CommonCell>` / `<TimeStampCell>`.
- Read-only span gets `onDoubleClick` (with cursor:text + tooltip "Double-click to edit") that fires `onStartAdhocEdit`.
- `CommonCell` extended with `autoFocus`, `onKeyDown` (Escape cancels, Enter blurs to commit), and onBlur that calls `onCommitAdhocEdit` when in ad-hoc mode.

**Behavior:**

- **Double-click any cell** in the jobs / shipments / vehicles import table → that one cell flips editable, cursor focused, current value selected.
- **Type → Enter** or **type → click elsewhere** → commits via the same Redux dispatch path the bulk-edit mode uses.
- **Escape** → discards the in-flight value and the cell flips back to read-only.
- The bulk **Edit / Save / Cancel** toolbar buttons still work exactly as before; double-clicking inside bulk-edit mode is a no-op (the cells are already editable).
- Tooltip "Double-click to edit" + a text-cursor hover hint surfaces the affordance.

Works for the standard text cells. The TimeStamp cell (date-picker) already had its own focus model — it just stays in the bulk-edit-only path until you specifically want ad-hoc date editing; happy to extend if you hit it.

 "new_string": "    // Prepend an empty data row (plus matching empty attached row) at\n    // index 0 of the given input type. Used by the \"Add Row\" toolbar\n    // button on the import table so the user can hand-author a stop\n    // without re-importing the whole CSV. Header is left untouched —\n    // the new row's column count matches the existing schema.\n    prependEmptyRow(state, type: InputType) {\n      const inputSet = state[type]\n      const colNum = inputSet.rawData.header.length\n      const attachedColNum = inputSet.rawData.attachedRows[0]?.length ?? 0\n      if (colNum === 0) {\n        // No header yet — nothing to seed a row against; bail.\n        return state\n      }\n      const emptyRow = Array(colNum).fill('')\n      const emptyAttached = Array(attachedColNum).fill('')\n      return {\n        ...state,\n        [type]: {\n          ...inputSet,\n          rawData: {\n            ...inputSet.rawData,\n            rows: [emptyRow, ...inputSet.rawData.rows],\n            attachedRows: [emptyAttached, ...inputSet.rawData.attachedRows],\n          },\n        },\n      }\n    },\n    clearMetaMapping(state) {"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T23:35:55.864Z)

Done.

**Summary of changes:**

- **`apps/route-planner-v2/models/input/input-core.ts`** — new reducer `prependEmptyRow(type)`. Builds an empty data row sized to match the existing header and a matching empty attached row, then unshifts both into `rows` / `attachedRows` for the given input type. No-op if there's no header yet.

- **`apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/data-mapper/data-mapper.tsx`** — new `PlaylistAddIcon` import, new `handleAddRow` handler that:
  1. Dispatches `prependEmptyRow(inputType)`.
  2. Flips the table into bulk-edit mode so every cell in the new (empty) row is immediately editable in one click.
  
  New **Add row** button added to the toolbar right after **Add attribute**. Disabled until the table has headers (otherwise there's nothing to seed an empty row against).

- **`messages/{en,es-MX,pt-BR,fr-CA}.json`** — added `dataMapper.addRow` key in all four locales.

**Behavior:**

- Click **Add row** on the jobs / shipments / vehicles import table → a blank row appears at index 0, the table enters bulk-edit mode.
- The user fills cells across the new row, then clicks **Save** (or **Cancel** to discard).
- The new row participates in all downstream flows (mapping, validation, deletion, CSV export, optimization) exactly like an imported row, because it lives in the same `rows`/`attachedRows` arrays.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-04T23:47:41.403Z)

The vertex/midpoint handles in `PreviewLassoEditOverlay` are absolutely positioned via `viewMap.project()`. When a polygon vertex sits outside the current viewport (the polygon extends past the visible map), the handle still renders — and because the overlay's container has no `overflow: hidden`, those handles spill onto whatever's next to the map (your table). Adding `overflow: hidden` to the overlay container clips them to the map area.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T00:04:17.592Z)

This already works end-to-end — no code change needed. Here's the full round-trip:

1. **Add row** — `prependEmptyRow(type)` (in `input-core.ts:543`) unshifts an empty row into `state[type].rawData.rows` and a matching empty entry into `attachedRows`.
2. **Edit cells** — `onCellChange` in `data-mapper.tsx:906` dispatches `setRawData(type, {header, rows, attachedRows})` with the updated arrays. The new row's edited values land in the same `rawData.rows`.
3. **Save** — when the user checks "Save this setup for future route planning" and clicks Generate, `input-preview-page.tsx:766` fires `saveInputSet(zones)`. That action (input-core.ts:2295) reads `rootState.inputCore.job/shipment/vehicle/depot` — the full `InputSet` for each type, which contains `rawData.rows` + `attachedRows` including the prepended row — and `saveInputConfig` (configure.ts:99) uploads the object straight to GCS, no filtering.
4. **Load** — on the next session, `loadInputConfiguration` (input-core.ts:2253) fetches the JSON from GCS and calls `setInputSet(type, inputData.job)` for each type, which spreads the saved `InputSet` back into state. The prepended row reappears at index 0 with its edited values.

The `prependEmptyRow` reducer landed directly in `state.[type].rawData`, which is the same shape `saveInputSet` already serializes wholesale — so it inherits persistence for free. If you tried it and a row vanished after save+reload, that's a bug worth surfacing; otherwise, you should already be seeing new rows survive the round-trip.

Used by the \"Add Row\" toolbar button\n    // on the import table so the user can hand-author a stop without\n    // re-importing the whole CSV.\n    //\n    // The new row's cell values are CLONED from whatever row currently\n    // sits at index 0 (which becomes index 1 after the prepend) — this\n    // gives the user sensible starting values instead of a blank row.\n    // The typical workflow is \"duplicate this stop and tweak the few\n    // fields that differ\" (a different address, a different time\n    // window). When the table has no existing rows, every cell falls\n    // back to empty string. Header is left untouched — the new row's\n    // column count matches the existing schema.\n    prependEmptyRow(state, type: InputType) {\n      const inputSet = state[type]\n      const colNum = inputSet.rawData.header.length\n      const attachedColNum = inputSet.rawData.attachedRows[0]?.length ?? 0\n      if (colNum === 0) {\n        // No header yet — nothing to seed a row against; bail.\n        return state\n      }\n      const templateRow = inputSet.rawData.rows[0]\n      const templateAttached = inputSet.rawData.attachedRows[0]\n      const newRow = templateRow\n        ? templateRow.slice()\n        : Array(colNum).fill('')\n      const newAttached = templateAttached\n        ? templateAttached.slice()\n        : Array(attachedColNum).fill('')\n      return {\n        ...state,\n        [type]: {\n          ...inputSet,\n          rawData: {\n            ...inputSet.rawData,\n            rows: [newRow, ...inputSet.rawData.rows],\n            attachedRows: [newAttached, ...inputSet.rawData.attachedRows],\n          },\n        },\n      }\n    },"

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T00:06:33.083Z)

Done.

**`apps/route-planner-v2/models/input/input-core.ts`** — `prependEmptyRow` now seeds the new row by cloning `rawData.rows[0]` (the row directly beneath the insertion point) and `rawData.attachedRows[0]`. `.slice()` produces a shallow copy so subsequent edits to either row don't mutate the other. Empty-table behavior is preserved (every cell falls back to `''` when there's no existing row to template from).

So when the user clicks **Add row**:
- Table already has data → new row at index 0 is a duplicate of the existing first row.
- Table is empty (header only) → new row is blank (same behavior as before).

The cloned values are just initial seeds — the existing per-cell editing (both ad-hoc double-click and bulk Edit mode) and the GCS persistence already established still apply to the new row exactly as before.

{

 "content": "import type {UserInfo} from '@ncc/common'\nimport type {IamUser} from '../types/iam-user'\n\n/**\n * Client-side impersonation.\n *\n * Demo-grade feature: an admin can pick another IAM user from the\n * admin/users page and \"impersonate\" them. The session JWT is\n * unchanged — the backend still sees the real admin — but the\n * frontend's permission gates read the IMPERSONATED user, so the UI\n * behaves as if that user were logged in.\n *\n * This is intentionally NOT a secure boundary. It's a \"view as\"\n * affordance for support and QA, not a way to actually take an\n * action under someone else's identity. The banner makes the\n * state visible at all times.\n */\n\nconst STORAGE_KEY = 'ncc-impersonation-v1'\n\n/**\n * Persisted shape. Stores just enough to reconstruct a `UserInfo`\n * for permission checks (employeeType role array, email, org).\n */\nexport type ImpersonationRecord = {\n  email: string\n  name: string\n  org: string\n  employeeType: string[]\n  /** Snapshot of the admin doing the impersonation, for the banner UI. */\n  adminEmail: string\n  /** Unix seconds — when impersonation was started. Surfaced in the\n   *  banner so the admin notices they've been in this mode for a while. */\n  startedAt: number\n}\n\nexport function readImpersonation(): ImpersonationRecord | null {\n  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null\n  try {\n    const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)\n    if (!raw) return null\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as ImpersonationRecord\n    if (!parsed || typeof parsed.email !== 'string') return null\n    return parsed\n  } catch {\n    return null\n  }\n}\n\nexport function writeImpersonation(record: ImpersonationRecord): void {\n  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return\n  try {\n    window.localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(record))\n    // Notify other tabs and the in-page provider — `storage` events\n    // only fire on OTHER tabs by spec, so we also dispatch a custom\n    // event so the same-tab listener picks up the change immediately.\n    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ncc-impersonation-change'))\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore storage failures (private mode, quota, etc.) */\n  }\n}\n\nexport function clearImpersonation(): void {\n  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return\n  try {\n    window.localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY)\n    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ncc-impersonation-change'))\n  } catch {\n    /* ignore */\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Convert an IAM directory entry into the runtime `UserInfo` shape\n * used by permission helpers. IAM's `role` is a single-role string\n * (e.g. 'admin' / 'owner' / 'viewer'); `employeeType` (the field\n * `isAdmin`/`isOwner`/`isViewer` check) is an array. We coerce\n * accordingly.\n */\nexport function iamUserToUserInfo(iam: IamUser): UserInfo {\n  const employeeType = iam.role ? [iam.role] : []\n  return {\n    email: iam.mail,\n    name: iam.sn || iam.mail,\n    org: iam.org,\n    employeeType,\n    isAnonymousUser: false,\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the runtime `UserInfo` for an impersonation record. The\n * impersonated user inherits the real admin's `org` (so API calls\n * still resolve correctly via the real JWT) but assumes the\n * impersonated user's employeeType / role for UI permission gates.\n */\nexport function impersonationToUserInfo(\n  record: ImpersonationRecord,\n): UserInfo {\n  return {\n    email: record.email,\n    name: record.name,\n    org: record.org,\n    employeeType: record.employeeType,\n    isAnonymousUser: false,\n  }\n}\n"
}

Permission\n   *  hooks (`useRoutePlannerPermissions`) read this. */\n  effectiveUser: UserInfo\n  /** Begin impersonating an IAM user. Self-impersonation is rejected. */\n  startImpersonating: (target: IamUser) => void\n  /** Exit impersonation and return to the real admin's identity. */\n  stopImpersonating: () => void\n}\n\nconst ImpersonationContext = createContext<ImpersonationContextValue | null>(null)\n\nexport function ImpersonationProvider({children}: {children: ReactNode}) {\n  const [appContext] = useContext(AppContext)\n  const realUser = appContext.currentUser\n  const [impersonation, setImpersonation] =\n    useState<ImpersonationRecord | null>(() => readImpersonation())\n\n  // Hydrate from localStorage on mount, then react to storage events\n  // (other tabs) and the same-tab custom event our writer dispatches.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    setImpersonation(readImpersonation())\n    const onChange = () => setImpersonation(readImpersonation())\n    window.addEventListener('storage', onChange)\n    window.addEventListener('ncc-impersonation-change', onChange)\n    return () => {\n      window.removeEventListener('storage', onChange)\n      window.removeEventListener('ncc-impersonation-change', onChange)\n    }\n  }, [])\n\n  // If the admin who STARTED impersonation differs from the current\n  // real user (e.g., logged out + back in as a different account),\n  // drop the stale record. Prevents one admin's impersonation state\n  // from following another admin into the app.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (impersonation && realUser.email && impersonation.adminEmail !== realUser.email) {\n      clearImpersonation()\n    }\n  }, [impersonation, realUser.email])\n\n  const startImpersonating = useCallback(\n    (target: IamUser) => {\n      if (!realUser.email) return\n      if (target.mail === realUser.email) return // can't impersonate self\n      const record: ImpersonationRecord = {\n        email: target.mail,\n        name: target.sn || target.mail,\n        org: target.org || realUser.org,\n        employeeType: iamUserToUserInfo(target).employeeType,\n        adminEmail: realUser.email,\n        startedAt: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),\n      }\n      writeImpersonation(record)\n      setImpersonation(record)\n    },\n    [realUser.email, realUser.org],\n  )\n\n  const stopImpersonating = useCallback(() => {\n    clearImpersonation()\n    setImpersonation(null)\n  }, [])\n\n  const effectiveUser = useMemo(\n    () => (impersonation ? impersonationToUserInfo(impersonation) : realUser),\n    [impersonation, realUser],\n  )\n\n  const value = useMemo<ImpersonationContextValue>(\n    () => ({\n      impersonation,\n      isImpersonating: !!impersonation,\n      realUser,\n      effectiveUser,\n      startImpersonating,\n      stopImpersonating,\n    }),\n    [impersonation, realUser, effectiveUser, startImpersonating, stopImpersonating],\n  )\n\n  return (\n    <ImpersonationContext.Provider value={value}>\n      {children}\n    </ImpersonationContext.Provider>\n  )\n}\n\nexport function useImpersonation(): ImpersonationContextValue {\n  const ctx = useContext(ImpersonationContext)\n  if (!ctx) {\n    throw new Error(\n      'useImpersonation must be used within an ImpersonationProvider',\n    )\n  }\n  return ctx\n}\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T14:47:54.146Z)

All wiring in place. Summary:

**New files (3):**

- **`utils/impersonation.ts`** — localStorage helpers (`readImpersonation`, `writeImpersonation`, `clearImpersonation`), `iamUserToUserInfo` and `impersonationToUserInfo` adapters. Persists `{email, name, org, employeeType, adminEmail, startedAt}`.

- **`context/impersonation-context.tsx`** — `ImpersonationProvider` + `useImpersonation()` hook. Exposes `{impersonation, isImpersonating, realUser, effectiveUser, startImpersonating, stopImpersonating}`. Listens to both `storage` (cross-tab) and a custom `ncc-impersonation-change` event (same-tab). Auto-clears the record if the real `currentUser` changes (different admin signs in).

- **`components/admin/impersonate-banner.tsx`** — sticky amber banner at `position:sticky; zIndex:1200` rendered once at the root. Shows "Viewing as `<email>` (real user: `<admin>`)" with an "Exit impersonation" button.

**Modified (5):**

- **`hooks/use-route-planner-permissions.ts`** — now reads `effectiveUser` from `useImpersonation()` instead of `currentUser` from `AppContext`. Every page that gates on `canManageUsers` / `canPlanRoutes` / `isViewerOnly` automatically respects impersonation through this single seam.

- **`components/admin/users-page.tsx`** — added `SwitchAccountIcon` button in the Actions column. Disabled for self, inactive accounts, or while already impersonating. Click → `startImpersonating(row)` + toast.

- **`context/providers.tsx`** — wraps the app in `ImpersonationProvider` and mounts `ImpersonateBanner` once. The banner only renders when impersonation is active.

- **`messages/{en,es-MX,pt-BR,fr-CA}.json`** — added `admin.users.impersonate*` keys (tooltip, ARIA labels, toast, banner copy) in all four locales. JSON valid.

**Behavior:**

- Admin opens `/admin/users` → clicks the new switch-accounts icon next to a user row → that user's role overlays the admin's permissions for the whole session.
- Banner sticks to the top of every page with "Exit" button.
- All permission-gated UI (e.g., Invite button, Edit role buttons, can-plan-routes gates) flip to whatever the impersonated user would see.
- Real backend identity (JWT cookie) is unchanged — every API call still authenticates as the admin. This is a UX overlay, not a security boundary, and the banner makes that visible.
- `ImpersonationContext` auto-discards the impersonation record if the underlying admin changes (e.g., logout + login as someone else).

Possible follow-ups if you want to take this further:
- Make impersonation a security boundary by adding a backend X-Impersonate-User header that the BFF validates against the admin's JWT.
- Persist impersonation across full page reloads of `/admin/users` (already does via localStorage).
- Add a confirmation dialog before starting impersonation if you'd prefer that extra step.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T15:29:14.498Z)

The 150 ms debounce I added only smooths the *filter* work — but `searchInput` state lives on the parent `RoutePanel`, so every keystroke re-renders the parent, which re-renders all 244 `RouteCard` children. That's the lag you're feeling.

Fix: isolate the input into its own tiny child component so its local state changes don't ripple up. The parent only re-renders when the debounced query lands in the Zustand store.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T15:32:05.614Z)

Three changes that compound:

**`apps/route-planner-v2/v3/features/solution/components/result-panel.tsx`**

1. **`RouteSearchInput` extracted as its own component** (lines around 130). Owns the local `value` state and the debounce timer. Subscribes only to `routeSearchQuery` / `setRouteSearchQuery` from the store. Keystrokes now re-render this ~50-line component instead of the 1000+ line `RoutePanel`.

2. **`RoutePanel` no longer holds the search input state.** It only reads `routeSearchQuery` from the Zustand store, which only updates after the 150 ms debounce. So `RoutePanel` doesn't re-render on every keystroke at all — only when typing pauses.

3. **`RouteCard` wrapped in `React.memo`.** Defensive: even when something else *does* re-render `RoutePanel` (selection churn, store updates), the 244 child cards now skip re-render unless their own `route` / `timezone` props change or their own Zustand subscriptions fire. The `route` references coming out of `displayRoutes` are stable (from the Zustand store's selector identity), so the memo bailout actually fires.

**Effect:**

- Per keystroke: only `<RouteSearchInput>` (one OutlinedInput) re-renders. Should feel instant.
- After 150 ms pause: store updates → parent re-renders once → filtered set + auto-select + map layers update — same single heavy pass as before, just no longer fighting the typing.
- Memo on `RouteCard` makes incidental re-renders during the heavy pass much cheaper (the 244 cards skip work when their props are unchanged).

If it's still laggy after this, the next culprit would be the route list being non-virtualized — 244 DOM nodes always mounted. Worth checking, but the input isolation should solve the typing-feels-stuck problem you're describing.

Both routes now use Basic auth and no `client_secret` appears anywhere in the body. Restart the Next dev server so the route handlers reload, and the OAuth flow should land cleanly.

**Diff summary:**

**Working demo (`~/workspace/poc_data/SCA/sf-oauth-demo/server.js`):**

```js
const basic = Buffer.from(`${CLIENT_ID}:${CLIENT_SECRET}`).toString('base64')
fetch(TOKEN_URL, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Basic ${basic}`,                  // ← creds here
    'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
  },
  body: new URLSearchParams({
    grant_type: 'authorization_code',
    code,
    redirect_uri: REDIRECT_URI,                       // ← NO id/secret in body
  }),
})
```

**Old v2 code (`callback/route.ts` and `token/route.ts`):**

```ts
fetch(`${loginUrl}/services/oauth2/token`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'},
  body: new URLSearchParams({
    grant_type: 'authorization_code',
    code, redirect_uri,
    client_id: credentials.clientId,                  // ← in body
    client_secret: credentials.clientSecret,           // ← in body — Salesforce rejects
  }),
})
```

**Now:**

```ts
const basic = Buffer.from(`${credentials.clientId}:${credentials.clientSecret}`).toString('base64')
fetch(`${loginUrl}/services/oauth2/token`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Basic ${basic}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded',
  },
  body: new URLSearchParams({grant_type, code, redirect_uri, ...maybeCodeVerifier}),
})
```

**Why this fixes it:** Salesforce Connected Apps configured with **"Require Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)"** or the newer **"Require secret for refresh token flow"** option reject the body-credentials form (returns `invalid_client` → surfaced to your UI as "invalid client credentials"). HTTP Basic auth is the universally-accepted path and matches the OAuth 2.0 spec recommendation.

If the Connected App in question doesn't have those options set, both forms *should* work — but since the demo using Basic works and the v2 using body fails on the exact same Connected App, the Connected App is clearly enforcing the stricter path.

Restart, retry the connect flow, and the token exchange should now mirror what the demo does. PKCE (`code_verifier`) and the optional env-var override for the secret are both preserved end-to-end.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T19:28:57.743Z)

Done. Restart the Next dev server so the constant reloads on the server side, then retry the connect.

**End-to-end flow now (no env var needed):**

1. `login/route.ts` → `SF_OAUTH_USE_PKCE` is true → `createPkcePair()` generates `code_verifier` (random 32 bytes, base64url) + `code_challenge` (SHA-256 of verifier, base64url).
2. `buildSalesforceAuthorizeUrl` appends `code_challenge` + `code_challenge_method=S256` to the `/services/oauth2/authorize` URL. ← **This is the fix for the `missing required code challenge` error.**
3. Pending state (including `codeVerifier`) is stashed in the in-memory store + the encrypted cookie.
4. Salesforce redirects back with `code`.
5. `callback/route.ts` → `exchangeCode` POSTs to `/services/oauth2/token` with `code_verifier` in the body and `Basic base64(clientId:clientSecret)` in the header (last turn's fix).
6. Salesforce verifies `SHA256(verifier) === stored challenge`, returns access + refresh tokens.

**Disable path** (if you ever need it for a Connected App that doesn't have the PKCE checkbox set): set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SF_OAUTH_PKCE=false` in `.env.local` and restart. But there's no real reason to — PKCE is just additional security on top of the regular code grant, and the Connected App accepts the extra params silently when the option isn't enforced.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T19:33:01.313Z)

File is clean. Restart Next so the routes reload, then attempt the connect once and check the dev-server console.

**Look for two `[sf-oauth]` log lines:**

```
[sf-oauth] token exchange { tokenUrl, clientIdPrefix, clientIdLength, clientSecretLength, clientSecretFromEnv, redirectUri, hasCodeVerifier, codeVerifierLength }
[sf-oauth] token response   { status, error, errorDescription }
```

**What to look at:**

1. **`clientSecretFromEnv: true`** — if you see this, your secret is coming from `SALESFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET` env var, not the UI form. That's almost always the culprit when "I changed the secret in the UI and it still fails." Check `.env`/`.env.local`/your shell env — `unset SALESFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET` if it's there from earlier testing, and restart the dev server.

2. **`clientIdPrefix`** — should be the first 8 chars of the **Consumer Key** of the Connected App that has PKCE enabled. If it doesn't match what you see in Setup → App Manager → View on the Connected App, you're hitting a different app than the one you configured.

3. **`tokenUrl`** — should be `https://<your-my-domain>.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token`. If it's `https://login.salesforce.com/...` instead, Salesforce will route to the wrong tenant and reject the credentials.

4. **`redirectUri`** — must EXACTLY match one of the callback URLs in the Connected App (Salesforce makes redirect_uri matching strict under PKCE). `http://localhost:4200/oauth/_callback` vs `http://127.0.0.1:4200/oauth/_callback` vs `http://localhost:4200/route-planner/api/integrations/salesforce/callback` are all DIFFERENT to Salesforce.

5. **`error: "invalid_client_credentials"`** with `clientSecretLength` of 0 or near-zero → the secret never made it to this code. If non-zero but still failing, it's a real secret mismatch.

Paste the log line back and I can pinpoint the exact failure. Most common cases when this error persists after switching transports: (a) wrong/regenerated secret, (b) the secret is coming from a stale env var, (c) the Consumer Key in the UI form belongs to a different Connected App than where you ticked the PKCE box.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T19:40:05.523Z)

All four locales valid. Summary of what was added and the parameter research behind each form:

---

## ServiceNow

**Auth path researched:** REST Table API at `{instanceUrl}/api/now/table/{tableName}`. Two supported auth modes:
- **OAuth 2.0** — register the app under *System OAuth → Application Registry*; use the resulting Client ID + Secret. The `password` grant is the simplest server-to-server path; `authorization_code` works for delegated user auth.
- **Basic auth** — any user with REST access and the `rest_service` role works without OAuth plumbing.

**Form fields (in `servicenow-import-panel.tsx`):**
| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Instance URL | `https://yourcompany.service-now.com` |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.0 / Basic toggle |
| Client ID / Client Secret | OAuth only — from System OAuth → Application Registry |
| Username / Password | OAuth password grant or Basic credentials |
| Table name | REST target — defaults to `wm_task` (Work Management) for jobs, `wm_order` for shipments, `cmdb_ci_vehicle` for vehicles |
| sysparm_query | ServiceNow encoded filter, e.g. `active=true^assignment_groupISNOTEMPTY` |
| sysparm_fields | Comma-separated field whitelist |

---

## Microsoft Dynamics 365

**Auth path researched:** Dataverse Web API at `{environmentUrl}/api/data/v9.2/{entitySet}`. Auth is Azure AD OAuth 2.0:
- Register an app in Azure AD → record **Tenant ID**, **Application (client) ID**, generate a **Client secret**.
- Grant the app Dataverse access (system administrator or custom security role mapped to the app's application user).
- Token endpoint: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/token`.
- Body: `grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=...&client_secret=...&scope={environmentUrl}/.default`.
- Use the returned `access_token` as a Bearer header against the Dataverse API.

**Form fields (in `dynamics-import-panel.tsx`):**
| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Environment URL | `https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com` (Web API path appended for you) |
| Tenant ID | Azure AD directory GUID |
| Application (client) ID | Azure AD app registration GUID |
| Client Secret | Corresponding secret from the app registration |
| Entity set | Plural OData name — defaults to `msdyn_workorders` (Field Service work orders) for jobs, `msdyn_workorderservicetasks` for shipments, `bookableresources` for vehicles |
| OData query | `$filter`, `$select`, `$expand` etc. |

---

## Files touched

**Created:**
- `components/input/import-source/servicenow-import-panel.tsx`
- `components/input/import-source/dynamics-import-panel.tsx`

**Modified:**
- `components/input/import-source/types.ts` — added `'servicenow' | 'dynamics'` to `ImportMethod`, new `ServiceNowImportSettings` and `DynamicsImportSettings` types, per-entity defaults (per-entity table/entitySet mapping).
- `components/input/import-source/import-source-cache.ts` — round-trips the two new settings blocks through localStorage.
- `components/input/import-source/import-source-panel.tsx` — dispatches to the new panels when method matches.
- `messages/{en,pt-BR,es-MX,fr-CA}.json` — full `importSource.servicenow` + `importSource.dynamics` namespaces (titles, "Coming soon" chips, info notices, every label + helper text). All four locales validate.

**Behavior parity:** Both new panels follow the existing SAP-panel pattern (UI scaffolding + "Coming soon" chip + info Alert). Settings are persisted to localStorage exactly like SAP/Salesforce/API settings — change tabs or reload, the form remembers what you entered. The actual outbound fetch / token exchange is the next step (the SAP panel is in the same state today). Happy to wire those up when you're ready — both are straightforward server-side actions following the Salesforce callback pattern you already have.

 "new_string": "'use client'\nimport {useMemo, useState} from 'react'\nimport {Autocomplete, Box, Button, Chip, TextField} from '@mui/material'\nimport FilterAltOutlined from '@mui/icons-material/FilterAltOutlined'\nimport {DateTimePicker} from '@mui/x-date-pickers'\nimport {AdapterDayjs} from '@mui/x-date-pickers/AdapterDayjs'\nimport {LocalizationProvider} from '@mui/x-date-pickers/LocalizationProvider'\nimport dayjs, {Dayjs} from 'dayjs'\nimport 'dayjs/locale/en'\nimport 'dayjs/locale/pt-br'\nimport 'dayjs/locale/es-mx'\nimport {useLocale, useTranslations} from 'next-intl'\nimport {useDispatch, useSelector} from 'react-redux'\nimport {Dispatch, RootState} from '../../../models/input/store'\n\n// Normalise a job/vehicle zone entry (string OR number) to a numeric\n// zone id for comparison against the zone option list. Returns null\n// when the value can't be parsed.\nfunction toZoneId(raw: unknown): number | null {\n  if (raw === null || raw === undefined || raw === '') return null\n  const n = typeof raw === 'number' ? raw : Number.parseInt(String(raw), 10)\n  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null\n}\n\nexport type ZoneOption = {id: number; label: string}\n\n// Build {id, label} options from the optimization input's zones.\n// Mirrors the analytics-side rebrand: \"Zone N\" → \"Territory N\" only\n// when the zone has a default name; free-text geofence names pass\n// through unchanged.\nexport function buildZoneOptions(\n  zones: Array<{id: number; name?: string}> | undefined,\n): ZoneOption[] {\n  if (!zones?.length) return []\n  return [...zones]\n    .map((z) => ({\n      id: z.id,\n      label: z.name?.trim() ? z.name : `Zone ${z.id}`,\n    }))\n    .sort((a, b) => a.id - b.id)\n}"
}

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/vehicle-filter-bar.tsx",
 "content": "'use client'\nimport {useMemo, useState} from 'react'\nimport {Autocomplete, Box, Button, Chip, TextField} from '@mui/material'\nimport FilterAltOutlined from '@mui/icons-material/FilterAltOutlined'\nimport {useTranslations} from 'next-intl'\nimport {useDispatch, useSelector} from 'react-redux'\nimport {Dispatch, RootState} from '../../../models/input/store'\nimport {buildZoneOptions, type ZoneOption} from './job-filter-bar'\n\n/**\n * Zone-only filter for the Vehicles preview table.\n *\n * A vehicle is kept when any of its `allowed_zones[]` entries\n * intersects with the selected-zone set. With no zones selected the\n * filter is inactive and every vehicle is included.\n *\n * Zones are normalised the same way `JobFilterBar` does — entries\n * stored as either `number` or `string` are coerced to numbers\n * before set comparison.\n */\nfunction toZoneId(raw: unknown): number | null {\n  if (raw === null || raw === undefined || raw === '') return null\n  const n = typeof raw === 'number' ? raw : Number.parseInt(String(raw), 10)\n  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null\n}\n\nexport function VehicleFilterBar() {\n  const t = useTranslations('vehicleFilter')\n  const dispatch = useDispatch<Dispatch>()\n  const vehicles = useSelector(\n    (state: RootState) => state.inputCore.output.vehicle ?? [],\n  )\n  const zonesInput = useSelector(\n    (state: RootState) => state.inputCore.output.zones,\n  )\n\n  const zoneOptions = useMemo(() => buildZoneOptions(zonesInput), [zonesInput])\n  const [selectedZones, setSelectedZones] = useState<ZoneOption[]>([])\n\n  // No zones in the input — no filter to render. Vehicles preview\n  // gets nothing on the toolbar; this matches the existing job\n  // toolbar behavior (the zone autocomplete just doesn't appear).\n  if (zoneOptions.length === 0) return null\n\n  const apply = () => {\n    const matching: number[] = []\n    if (selectedZones.length === 0) {\n      vehicles.forEach((_v, index) => matching.push(index))\n      dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedVehicles(matching)\n      return\n    }\n    const zoneIdSet = new Set(selectedZones.map((z) => z.id))\n    vehicles.forEach((vehicle: any, index: number) => {\n      const allowed = Array.isArray(vehicle.allowed_zones)\n        ? vehicle.allowed_zones\n        : []\n      const overlaps = allowed.some((z: unknown) => {\n        const id = toZoneId(z)\n        return id !== null && zoneIdSet.has(id)\n      })\n      if (overlaps) matching.push(index)\n    })\n    dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedVehicles(matching)\n  }\n\n  const clear = () => {\n    setSelectedZones([])\n    dispatch.inputPreview.setSelectedVehicles(vehicles.map((_, i) => i))\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Box\n      sx={{\n        display: 'flex',\n        gap: 1,\n        alignItems: 'center',\n        flexWrap: 'wrap',\n        mb: 1.5,\n        p: 1.5,\n        bgcolor: 'rgba(244, 244, 247, 1)',\n        borderRadius: 1,\n      }}\n    >\n      <FilterAltOutlined sx={{color: 'text.secondary'}} />\n      <Autocomplete<ZoneOption, true>\n        multiple\n        size=\"small\"\n        options={zoneOptions}\n        value={selectedZones}\n        onChange={(_e, next) => setSelectedZones(next)}\n        getOptionLabel={(opt) => opt.label}\n        isOptionEqualToValue={(a, b) => a.id === b.id}\n        renderTags={(tags, getTagProps) =>\n          tags.map((opt, i) => (\n            <Chip\n              size=\"small\"\n              label={opt.label}\n              {...getTagProps({index: i})}\n              key={opt.id}\n            />\n          ))\n        }\n        renderInput={(params) => (\n          <TextField {...params} label={t('allowedZonesLabel')} />\n        )}\n        sx={{minWidth: 280, maxWidth: 420, flex: '1 1 280px'}}\n      />\n      <Button variant=\"contained\" size=\"small\" onClick={apply}>\n        {t('apply')}\n      </Button>\n      <Button variant=\"text\" size=\"small\" onClick={clear}>\n        {t('clear')}\n      </Button>\n    </Box>\n  )\n}\n"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T20:00:13.342Z)

Done.

**Summary:**

- **`components/input/input-preview-page/job-filter-bar.tsx`** — added a Zone multi-select (MUI `Autocomplete` with `multiple`) between the time-window pickers and the Apply button. Reads zones from `state.inputCore.output.zones`, only renders when the input has at least one zone defined. Filter matches jobs whose `zones[]` intersects the selected set. Diagnostic log + Clear handler updated. Exports `buildZoneOptions` + `ZoneOption` so the vehicle bar can reuse them.

- **`components/input/input-preview-page/vehicle-filter-bar.tsx`** *(new)* — same pattern as the job filter but with a single Zone multi-select labeled "Allowed zones". Filters vehicles whose `allowed_zones[]` intersects the selected set. Empty selection = include all vehicles. Renders nothing if the input has no zones, mirroring how the job filter's autocomplete hides itself in that case.

- **`components/input/input-preview-page/preview.tsx`** — imports `VehicleFilterBar`; renders it on the Vehicles tab (line right after the existing `tabValue === 'job' && <JobFilterBar />`).

- **`messages/{en,pt-BR,es-MX,fr-CA}.json`** — added `jobFilter.zonesLabel` and the new `vehicleFilter` namespace with `allowedZonesLabel`, `apply`, `clear`. JSON valid across all four.

**Behavior:**

- Jobs tab: filter bar now has `ID | Description | Time window from | Time window to | Zones | Apply | Clear`. Selecting "Zone 4" + "Zone 7" + clicking Apply keeps only jobs whose `zones[]` includes either id.
- Vehicles tab: filter bar with `Allowed zones | Apply | Clear`. Selecting "Zone 4" keeps vehicles whose `allowed_zones[]` includes id 4.
- Both autocompletes display Chips for selected zones, support multi-select, search-as-you-type, and clear-all via the autocomplete's built-in × button.
- The Zone column you screenshotted (showing `4`, `0`, `8`, etc.) is the same field the filter targets, so the column data and the filter agree.

Capped so jumbo clusters\n        // don't blow out.\n        return Math.min(48, 12 + 6 * Math.sqrt(n))\n      },\n      radiusUnits: 'pixels',\n      getFillColor: (d: any) => {\n        const zoneRef = d.properties?.zoneId\n        if (zoneRef !== null && zoneRef !== undefined) {\n          const color = zoneNameToColor[String(zoneRef)]\n          if (color) return [color[0], color[1], color[2], 220]\n        }\n        // Neutral fallback when clustered jobs span multiple zones (or\n        // none have a zone yet).\n        return [120, 120, 120, 220]\n      },\n      getLineColor: [255, 255, 255, 230],\n      lineWidthMinPixels: 1.5,\n      onHover: (info: any) => {\n        if (info?.object) {\n          // Custom marker so the tooltip render branch can identify\n          // this as a pin-cluster (vs an input feature / zone). Counts\n          // as a \"non-input\" hover so the existing dedup still works.\n          info.object.popupType = 'pinCluster'\n        }\n        setHoverInfo(info?.object ? info : undefined)\n      },\n    })\n  }, [clusters, zoneNameToColor])"
}

## 2. Demo login screen for route-planner-v2

Same credentials as SCA / GLWAS demos (`[EMAIL]` / `[REDACTED_SECRET]`, overridable via `DEMO_USER` / `DEMO_PASS` env vars). After sign-in, the user is sent to `/route-planner`.

**Created:**

- **`app/demo-login/page.tsx`** — MUI-styled login form (matches the rest of route-planner-v2). Reads `?next=` from the URL so the middleware can bounce users to login and back to the original deep-link. POSTs to the API below; on success, full-page navigates to `next` (default `/route-planner`).

- **`app/api/demo-login/route.ts`** — POST validates email/password against `DEMO_USER` / `DEMO_PASS` env vars (defaults match the SCA demo). On match, sets an HttpOnly cookie `rpv2_demo_auth=[REDACTED]` (7-day TTL). DELETE clears the cookie for logout. Cookie name is namespaced (`rpv2_…`) so it doesn't collide with `sca_demo_auth` if you host both demos on the same eTLD.

**Modified:**

- **`middleware.ts`** — added the demo gate at the very top:
  - When the demo cookie is missing or wrong, page requests redirect to `/demo-login?next=<original>`; API requests get a clean `401 unauthorized` so fetch callers handle their own error UI.
  - Exempt paths (must remain reachable without the cookie): `/demo-login`, `/api/demo-login`, OAuth callbacks (`/oauth/_callback`, `/auth/callback`, `/callback`, `/share-callback`), and `/dev-login` (the existing IAM auto-login flow).
  - All other existing middleware behavior (Salesforce callback rewrite, legacy solution redirect, dev-login bounce, common IAM middleware) runs unchanged after the demo gate passes.

**One caveat to be aware of:** the existing middleware matcher excludes `/api/...` from running middleware entirely, so the demo gate does NOT protect server-side API routes — only browser-facing pages. That matches what the user-facing demo gate needs (keep strangers from loading the UI). If you want APIs gated too, say the word and I'll extend the matcher and add the same cookie check for `/api/...`.

**Env overrides per deploy:**
- `DEMO_USER` — overrides email check
- `DEMO_PASS` — overrides password check
- `DEMO_AUTH_TOKEN` — overrides the opaque cookie value (rotate to invalidate all existing sessions)

Restart the Next dev server (the middleware module is server-side) and hit any route — you should land on `/route-planner/demo-login`. Sign in with `[EMAIL]` / `[REDACTED_SECRET]` and you'll be sent to `/route-planner`.

Done. Hard-refresh `/route-planner/demo-login` (or restart the dev server) so the page bundle picks up the new fetch URL.

**Why the 404 happened:**
The Next.js config sets `basePath: '/route-planner'`, so the API route handler `app/api/demo-login/route.ts` is served at `/route-planner/api/demo-login`. Browser `fetch()` does **not** auto-prepend the basePath — `fetch('/api/demo-login')` hit `http://localhost:4200/api/demo-login` (no `/route-planner`), where nothing exists.

**Fix:**
`app/demo-login/page.tsx` now uses `${ROUTE_PLANNER_BASE_PATH}/api/demo-login` so the URL is `/route-planner/api/demo-login` regardless of where the page is mounted. It also imports `ROUTE_PLANNER_BASE_PATH` for the `next` default redirect target (instead of hardcoding the string), so if anyone ever changes `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH`, the login page stays in sync.

After reload you should see the POST hit `http://localhost:4200/route-planner/api/demo-login` in devtools, return `200`, set the `rpv2_demo_auth` cookie, and the page should navigate to `/route-planner`.

**Behavior now:**

- Hit `http://localhost:4200/` (or any URL outside the basePath) → middleware bounces you to `/route-planner/demo-login?next=/` → sign in → `resolveNext('/')` returns `/route-planner` → land on the app entry.

The sanitizer also blocks any cross-origin redirect attempt (anything that doesn't start with `/`) so a malicious `?next=https://evil.com` can't smuggle the user off-site post-login.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-05T23:18:09.807Z)

Done.

**`apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/preview-map/preview-map.tsx` — `zonedJobLayer`:**

- Was `pickable: false` — picking was expected to fall through to the job `IconLayer` underneath. Problem: the IconLayer's PNG has transparent pixels around the visible blue dot, and deck.gl picks against opaque pixels. The visible "brown dot" at street zoom is the `zonedJobLayer` (the colored zone-membership overlay drawn on top), and the cursor's center often lands on a transparent edge of the icon below — so nothing got picked.
- Now `pickable: true`. The layer's `onHover` looks up the matching job by id from `output.job`, builds a synthetic `Feature` with the same rich property set the IconLayer would have produced (`id`, `description`, `location`, `pickup`, `delivery`, `service`, `setup`, `skills`, `timeWindows`, `Zone`), tags it `popupType: 'input'`, and calls `setHoverInfo`.
- The tooltip render branch is unchanged — it still routes `popupType === 'input'` to `MapTooltip → InputTooltip`. The tooltip now displays the full job rows on hover.

So the behavior after this:
- Hover a cluster → "N jobs in cluster" tooltip (unchanged).
- Hover an individual dot (the colored zone-dot you see in the screenshot) → full job tooltip with id, description, time windows, zone, etc.

The deduplication-free `onInputHover` wrapper from the previous turn still handles the IconLayer path in case the cursor happens to land squarely on the opaque part of the icon. So both code paths reach the tooltip.

4. Errors and fixes:

   - **`react_map_gl Map is not a constructor` runtime error in preview-map.tsx**:
     - Cause: `import Map from 'react-map-gl'` shadowed built-in Map. `new Map<unknown, any>()` tried to construct the react-map-gl component.
     - Fix: Replaced with `Record<string, any>` and `String(job.id)` keying.

   - **Demo login 404**:
     - Cause: `fetch('/api/demo-login')` hit `http://localhost:4200/api/demo-login` (no basePath), but the API route is mounted at `/route-planner/api/demo-login` due to `basePath: '/route-planner'`.
     - Fix: Used explicit `${ROUTE_PLANNER_BASE_PATH}/api/demo-login` in fetch.

   - **Post-login redirect went to base URL not /route-planner**:
     - Cause: Middleware passed `next=/` when user originally hit root; after login `window.location.href = '/'` had no page.
     - Fix: `resolveNext()` sanitizer ensures returned path is under `/route-planner` basePath; defaults to base path when not.

   - **Preview map tooltip not showing after filter applied**:
     - Cause: Shared lib `createHoverHandlers().onInputHover` had module-state `lastHoveredId` dedup that persisted across renders. After filter applies, cursor re-enters map over same icon id and dedup short-circuits before tooltip renders.
     - Fix: Replaced with inline wrapper that directly sets `popupType: 'input'` and `setHoverInfo(info)` with no dedup state.

   - **Tooltip only on clusters not individual pins**:
     - Cause: `zonedJobLayer` (colored zone-dot overlay) was `pickable: false`. The IconLayer underneath had transparent pixels around the visible icon, so cursor often landed on transparent edges = no pick.
     - Fix: Made `zonedJobLayer` pickable with onHover that looks up the matching job from `output.job` by id and synthesizes a Feature with rich properties.

   - **Salesforce `invalid_client_credentials`**:
     - First tried Basic auth based on demo. Still failed.
     - Per Salesforce PKCE docs, client_id + client_secret go in body. Reverted to body-credentials; added diagnostic console.log of clientId prefix, secret length, env-var presence, redirect URI, codeVerifier presence.

   - **Salesforce `missing required code challenge`**:
     - Cause: PKCE was opt-in via `NEXT_PUBLIC_SF_OAUTH_PKCE === 'true'`.
     - Fix: Flipped to opt-out (default true), comparing `!== 'false'`.

   - **Search box performance with 244 routes**:
     - Initial fix (150ms debounce) didn't fully fix because parent RoutePanel re-rendered on every keystroke and 244 RouteCard children re-rendered too.
     - Final fix: Extracted `RouteSearchInput` as its own component with local state + debounced store update; wrapped `RouteCard` in `React.memo`.

   - **User rollback on zone label change**: User said "rollback that last change not what I wanted" — restored `ZONE_LABEL_HIDE_ZOOM = 13` gate after I had removed it.

   The most recent work was on persisting zone filter chip state across tab switches in the preview screen. The user reported: "in preview screen, set zone filters and you can see the jobs being filtered. Go to the vehicles tab and then return to jobs tab. Zones are still filtered but the zone selector doesn't show the previously selected zones".

   I diagnosed: `JobFilterBar`/`VehicleFilterBar` keep `selectedZones` as local `useState`. When the user navigates away the component unmounts and state is lost. The filter RESULT (`selectedJobs`/`selectedVehicles`) lives in Redux so the actual filtered set persists, creating the visible mismatch.

### USER (2026-06-07T14:37:00.185Z)

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, call ScheduleWakeup** with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks past the 5-minute cache window are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 — the Monitor remains the wake signal; this only resets the safety net.
6. **To stop the loop**, omit the ScheduleWakeup call and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context).

 "content": "'use client'\nimport {PickingInfo} from '@deck.gl/core/typed'\nimport {useTranslations} from 'next-intl'\nimport {formatTimeWindow} from '@ncc/route-planner-components'\n// Reuse the shared map-tooltip stylesheet so the localized variant\n// matches the rest of the input/output popups visually. The lib\n// exports the SCSS module from the same path as the component.\nimport sharedStyles from '@ncc/route-planner-components/src/lib/components/map-tooltip.module.scss'\n\ntype Props = {\n  hoverInfo: Pick<PickingInfo, 'object' | 'x' | 'y'>\n  timezone?: string\n}\n\n/**\n * Drop-in replacement for the shared `InputTooltip` used by the\n * preview-map hover popup, with the field labels translated through\n * next-intl. The shared lib's tooltip uses raw property keys as labels\n * — fine for English-only consumers, but the preview map in this app\n * needs to render in the user's chosen locale.\n *\n * We keep the rendering / property iteration shape identical so the\n * popup matches the rest of the input/output tooltips visually.\n */\nexport function LocalizedInputTooltip({hoverInfo, timezone}: Props) {\n  const t = useTranslations('inputTooltip')\n  if (!hoverInfo.object) return null\n  const info = (hoverInfo.object as any).properties as Record<string, unknown>\n  if (!info) return null\n\n  // Translate a property-name → display label. Falls back to the raw\n  // key when no entry exists in the namespace so unforeseen fields\n  // still surface something readable instead of crashing on missing\n  // keys.\n  const labelFor = (key: string): string => {\n    try {\n      return t(key as never)\n    } catch {\n      return key\n    }\n  }\n\n  const contents: {label: string; value: any}[] = []\n  for (const key of Object.keys(info)) {\n    const raw = (info as any)[key]\n    if (raw === undefined || raw === null || raw === '') continue\n    if (key === 'timeWindows' && Array.isArray(raw)) {\n      contents.push({\n        label: labelFor('timeWindows'),\n        value: raw\n          .map((w: any) => formatTimeWindow(w, timezone ?? ''))\n          .join('\\n'),\n      })\n    } else if (key === 'timeWindow' && Array.isArray(raw)) {\n      contents.push({\n        label: labelFor('timeWindow'),\n        value: formatTimeWindow(raw as number[], timezone ?? ''),\n      })\n    } else if (key === 'capacity' || key === 'breaks') {\n      const stringValue =\n        typeof raw === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(raw) : String(raw)\n      contents.push({label: labelFor(key), value: stringValue})\n    } else {\n      contents.push({label: labelFor(key), value: raw})\n    }\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div\n      className={sharedStyles['nb-popup']}\n      style={{left: hoverInfo.x, top: hoverInfo.y}}\n    >\n      <div className=\"popup__content\">\n        {contents.map((content) => (\n          <div\n            className={sharedStyles['popup__content__item']}\n            key={content.label}\n          >\n            <div className={sharedStyles['popup__content__item__label']}>\n              {content.label}\n            </div>\n            <div className={sharedStyles['popup__content__item__value']}>\n              {String(content.value)}\n            </div>\n          </div>\n        ))}\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n"

The shared library wasn't touched, so `route-planner-viewer` (which uses `MapTooltip` but has no next-intl provider) is unaffected.

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, call ScheduleWakeup** with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks past the 5-minute cache window are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 — the Monitor remains the wake signal; this only resets the safety net.
6. **To stop the loop**, omit the ScheduleWakeup call and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context).

### CLAUDE (2026-06-08T13:27:34.118Z)
