## What this does

When the user toggles **Edit** on in the data mapper for jobs, shipments, or vehicles (the toggle is the existing `isTableEditable` in `data-mapper.tsx`), a narrow leading column appears with a trash icon per row. Clicking it pops the localized confirmation dialog; on confirm, the row is removed via the existing `inputCore.deleteData({type: inputType, indexes: [rowIndex]})` reducer — the same path the preview-screen bulk-delete uses, so it stays consistent with the rest of the input state (rawData rows, attachedRows, and output[type] are all spliced together).

## Files changed

- `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/data-mapper/data-mapper-table.tsx` — imported `IconButton`/`Tooltip` from `@ncc/ui` and `useTranslations` from `next-intl`, added `handleDeleteRow(rowIndex)` and a `ROW_ACTIONS_COL_WIDTH` constant. Prepended a sticky leading `TableCell` in both the header and each virtualized row when `isEditing` is true. Cell-index math elsewhere (`isTimestamp(cellIndex, …)`, `isAttribute: cellIndex >= columns.length`) is unchanged because the actions cell sits outside the `row.map`.
- `apps/route-planner-v2/messages/{en,pt-BR,es-MX,fr-CA,pl-PL}.json` — added `dataMapper.deleteRowTooltip`, `dataMapper.deleteRowConfirmTitle`, `dataMapper.deleteRowConfirmBody`.

## Behavior notes

- **No new column when edit is off** — the leading cell is gated on `isEditing`, so the read-only view keeps its original column layout. Cell indices for the data columns don't shift, so timestamp detection, attribute-column detection, and the existing ad-hoc double-click edit all keep working unchanged.
- **Same delete reducer as the preview screen** — uses `dispatch.inputCore.deleteData` with a single-element `indexes` array. That reducer already syncs `rawData.rows`, `attachedRows`, and `output[type]` together, so geocoded coordinates and any attribute-column data for the removed row also go away.
- **Confirms before deleting** — uses the existing `confirm` helper from `@ncc/common/client`, matching the pattern used for "Delete attribute" in the same file. The strings localize through the existing `dataMapper` namespace.
- **Depots also use this table** but the user only asked for jobs/shipments/vehicles. Since `DataMapperTable` is shared, depots automatically get the same affordance. If you want to exclude depots specifically, let me know and I'll gate the actions column on `inputType !== 'depot'`.

The dev server (port 4200) is still running from earlier — toggle Edit on a jobs/shipments/vehicles tab in the mapper, hover a row, and the trash icon should appear in the new leftmost column.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-08T13:33:49.882Z)

## What this does

When the user has mapped any source column to the optimization **`id`** field (jobs / shipments / vehicles / depots — same code path), a search field appears above the data-mapper table.

As they type, every row whose ID cell contains the query (case-insensitive substring) is:
1. **Floated to the top of the view** — without removing the non-matching rows; the user can still scroll down to see everything.
2. **Tinted pale yellow** so matches stand out even when many of them are bunched at the top.

A small "N matches" / "No matches" hint shows next to the field while a query is active. Clearing the field (× icon or empty input) restores the original order.

When no source column is mapped to `id`, the search field is hidden — and if the user unmaps the ID column while a query is active, the query state self-clears.

## Files changed

- `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/data-mapper/data-mapper-table.tsx` — added `searchQuery` state, looked up the mapped ID column via `mapConfig.dataMappings.find(d => d.value === 'id')`, computed `viewOrder` (matching rows first, then the rest) and `matchSet` (rows that should render the highlight tint). The `TableVirtuoso` now consumes `viewOrder` (an array of original row indices) instead of `innerRows`; `itemContent` receives the original index as its second arg, looks the row up with `innerRows[rowIndex]`, and passes `rowIndex` unchanged to every downstream consumer. That preserves all existing semantics for edit state, delete dispatch, highlight, ad-hoc edit, and scroll-into-view (`#cell-{rowIndex}-{cellIndex}` IDs still resolve because they're keyed on the original index).
- `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/data-mapper/data-mapper-cell.tsx` — added optional `isSearchMatch` prop. In `getHighlightColor()`, error-row red wins, search-match pale yellow comes next, then the zebra stripe falls through. So a validation-error match still renders red.
- `apps/route-planner-v2/messages/{en,pt-BR,es-MX,fr-CA,pl-PL}.json` — added `dataMapper.searchByIdPlaceholder`, `dataMapper.searchByIdClear`, and `dataMapper.searchByIdMatchCount` (ICU plural — and Polish gets the `few`/`many`/`other` plural categories it needs for grammatically correct counts).

## Behavior notes

- **No mutation of the underlying store** — sorting is purely view-side. Deleting a matching row from the reordered view still hits the correct underlying index because `rowIndex` is the original. The delete column added previously and the search work together — `handleDeleteRow(rowIndex)` always dispatches with the store-side index.
- **Substring + case-insensitive** — matches `Search by ID` typing of `pada-04` against `STACJA-0049` style IDs without forcing the user to remember casing. Wildcard syntax isn't supported (kept it simple); preview-screen filter still has the `*` pattern matcher for power users.
- **Stable React keys** — `key={`${rowIndex}-${cellIndex}`}` is keyed on the original row index, so when matches float to the top, React reuses the existing DOM nodes for each row rather than tearing them down. Editing state survives a search-reorder.
- **The leading edit-mode action column** sits to the left of the data columns and is untouched by the reorder; the delete button still operates on the correct underlying row.

Try it: map an "ID" column on the jobs (or shipments/vehicles) import screen, then start typing in the search field above the table — matches should bubble to the top with a yellow tint, "N matches" badge updates live, and clearing the field restores the original ordering.

 "content": "'use client'\n/**\n * Shared client for the NextBillion.ai discover endpoint used to back\n * any address-autocomplete UI in this app. Both the row-edit dialog\n * (`AddressAutocomplete`) and the geocode-preview cell inline\n * autocomplete consume this hook so they speak to the same host with\n * the same auth and debouncing.\n *\n *   GET https://<DISCOVER_HOST>/h/discover?q=<query>&limit=5&key=<apiKey>\n *\n * The user-supplied `currentApiKey.kid` already used for map tile URLs\n * authenticates this call — no extra auth wiring needed.\n */\n\nimport {useContext, useEffect, useState} from 'react'\nimport {AppContext} from '@ncc/common/client'\nimport {useDebounce} from 'use-debounce'\n\n// Discover always hits production regardless of env — staging\n// doesn't expose the discover endpoint reliably, and the\n// user-supplied API key is the same across envs for this product.\nexport const DISCOVER_HOST = 'api.nextbillion.io'\nexport const DISCOVER_MIN_QUERY_LENGTH = 3\nexport const DISCOVER_DEBOUNCE_MS = 250\n\nexport type DiscoverItem = {\n  title: string\n  id?: string\n  position: {lat: number; lng: number}\n  address?: {label?: string}\n}\n\nexport type UseDiscoverSearchResult = {\n  options: DiscoverItem[]\n  loading: boolean\n  /** True when the query was below the minimum-length threshold and the\n   *  request was therefore skipped. UI can use this to show a hint\n   *  (\"Search address…\") instead of \"No matches\". */\n  belowThreshold: boolean\n}\n\n/**\n * Debounced server-side address search. Returns the suggestion list\n * for the trimmed query, or an empty list when the query is too\n * short / the API key is missing / the request errored.\n *\n * @param query raw input the user is typing\n * @param opts.skip when true, no request is fired (useful when the\n *   field is closed or the user just picked a value and we don't\n *   want to re-search the same string)\n */\nexport function useDiscoverSearch(\n  query: string,\n  opts?: {skip?: boolean},\n): UseDiscoverSearchResult {\n  const [{currentApiKey}] = useContext(AppContext)\n  const [debouncedInput] = useDebounce(query, DISCOVER_DEBOUNCE_MS)\n  const [options, setOptions] = useState<DiscoverItem[]>([])\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)\n\n  const trimmed = debouncedInput.trim()\n  const belowThreshold = trimmed.length < DISCOVER_MIN_QUERY_LENGTH\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (opts?.skip || belowThreshold || !currentApiKey?.kid) {\n      setOptions([])\n      setLoading(false)\n      return\n    }\n    const controller = new AbortController()\n    setLoading(true)\n    const url = `https://${DISCOVER_HOST}/h/discover?q=${encodeURIComponent(\n      trimmed,\n    )}&limit=5&key=${encodeURIComponent(currentApiKey.kid)}`\n    fetch(url, {signal: controller.signal})\n      .then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : Promise.reject(r)))\n      .then((data) => {\n        const items: DiscoverItem[] = Array.isArray(data?.items)\n          ? data.items\n          : []\n        setOptions(items)\n      })\n      .catch((err) => {\n        if (controller.signal.aborted) return\n        // Surface the error to console; the user just sees an empty\n        // option list — same behavior as the rest of the geocoder.\n        // eslint-disable-next-line no-console\n        console.warn('[useDiscoverSearch] discover request failed', err)\n        setOptions([])\n      })\n      .finally(() => {\n        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setLoading(false)\n      })\n    return () => controller.abort()\n  }, [trimmed, currentApiKey?.kid, opts?.skip, belowThreshold])\n\n  return {options, loading, belowThreshold}\n}\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-06-08T13:50:07.223Z)

All five locales already have the strings the new component needs.

## What this does

When the user clicks an address in the **Review Geocoded Addresses** table to edit it, the plain `<InputBase>` is replaced by a MUI `<Autocomplete>` backed by the NextBillion.ai **discover** endpoint:

- Typing 3+ characters triggers `GET https://api.nextbillion.io/h/discover?q=<query>&limit=5&key=<currentApiKey.kid>` (debounced 250ms, cancelled on each new keystroke via `AbortController`).
- The 5 best suggestions render in the dropdown. While the request is in flight a small spinner shows in the input's end adornment, and the dropdown shows the localized "Searching address…" hint; an empty result set shows "No matches" (both already translated in all five locales via the existing `editRow.addressSearch` / `editRow.addressNoResults` keys).
- Picking a suggestion populates **address, lat, and lng** in one update — the user goes straight from typing to a valid geocoded row without having to click **Retry Geocoding**. The picked title is taken from `address.label` if present, falling back to `title`.
- If the user types free text and tabs out without picking, the existing fallback fires: the new address is stored, `lat`/`lng` are cleared, and the row joins the "needs retry geocoding" set (same behavior as before).
- The lat/lng cells still use the plain `<InputBase>` — unchanged.

## Files changed/added

- `apps/route-planner-v2/hooks/use-discover-search.ts` — new. Extracts the debounced discover-endpoint request into a hook with stable types (`DiscoverItem`) and constants (`DISCOVER_HOST`, `DISCOVER_MIN_QUERY_LENGTH`, `DISCOVER_DEBOUNCE_MS`). Handles `AbortController` cleanup, the < 3-char skip, and the missing-API-key skip.
- `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/geocode-preview/address-edit-cell.tsx` — new. Inline autocomplete tailored for the table cell: no floating label, transparent border that turns blue on focus, slim padding, spinner in the end adornment. `onPick(item)` for the happy path, `onBlur(value)` for the free-text fallback.
- `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/geocode-preview/geoccode-preview-table.tsx` — swapped the `EditCell` render for the address field with `AddressEditCell`, added `handleAddressPick(rowIndex, item)` that writes `{address, lat, lng}` in one `onRowChange` and marks the row as updated. Lat/Lng cell editing is untouched.
- `apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/input-preview-page/address-autocomplete.tsx` — refactored the dialog-style autocomplete to consume the new hook so both call sites share one `DiscoverItem` type and one request implementation. Re-exports `DiscoverItem` so `edit-row-dialog.tsx`'s existing import path keeps working unchanged.

## Behavior notes

- **Auth** uses the same `currentApiKey.kid` from `AppContext` that the map tiles use, so no new env wiring or BFF route is needed. If the API key isn't loaded yet, the hook skips the request and the dropdown stays empty.
- **Production host pinned** to `api.nextbillion.io` (same as the dialog-style autocomplete) — staging doesn't reliably expose `/h/discover` and the user-supplied API key is consistent across envs for this product.
- **Skip while just-picked** — after a pick, the hook is told to skip until the input value diverges from the picked title, so picking a suggestion doesn't immediately reissue a search for the same string.
- **Race-safe** — each query installs an `AbortController` and aborts the previous one on the next keystroke. A late response with `signal.aborted` skips its setState.
- **No new translation keys needed** — the new component reuses `editRow.addressSearch` and `editRow.addressNoResults` which are already translated in en/pt-BR/es-MX/fr-CA/pl-PL.

Try it: open the Review Geocoded Addresses dialog, click any address (e.g. "GRU" in row 1 from your screenshot), and start typing — suggestions should populate within a quarter-second of you stopping, and picking one snaps the address + coords into the row in a single update.

### CLAUDE (2026-06-08T13:53:59.297Z)

 "replace_all": false,

### CLAUDE (2026-06-08T13:54:05.977Z)

## Root cause

`apps/route-planner-v2/components/input/geocode-preview/geocode-preview-modal.tsx:327`

```ts
selectedRowIndex={selectedRowIndex || -1}
```

The `selectedRowIndex` state is `number | null` (initialized to `null`). The `|| -1` was meant to convert `null` → `-1` before passing into `GeocodePreviewMap` (whose prop type is `number`, not nullable). But `||` treats **`0` as falsy too**, so clicking the very first row set `selectedRowIndex = 0` in the modal, then passed `-1` down to the map. The map's flyTo effect at `geocode-preview-map.tsx:164` then evaluated `geocodeRows[-1]` → `undefined` → skipped flyTo. Every other row index (`1`, `2`, …) is truthy and worked fine.

## Fix

Switched to `??` (nullish coalescing), which only converts `null` / `undefined` and leaves `0` intact. One-line change. Now clicking row 1 passes `0` through and the map flyTo effect fires.
